roster.name: Ja'Marr Chase
roster.outlook: Ja'Marr Chase and the Bengals travel to square off against the Steelers' second-ranked pass defense in Week 3. Pittsburgh is allowing just 15.5 fantasy points per game to WRs and is one of six teams that have yet to give up a receiving TD to the position. Chase will surely put that to the test, as he's coming off a 7-75-2 receiving line on nine targets in Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. Across two outings versus the division-rival Steelers in 2025, Chase registered a 19-191-1 line on 33 targets, so Joe Burrow will continue to feed his star wideout regardless of the matchup.

roster.name: Derrick Henry
roster.outlook: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.

roster.name: Colston Loveland
roster.outlook: Colston Loveland will look to turn things around as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Loveland disappointed again in Week 2, catching just one of three targets for three yards against the Vikings. The second-year tight end now has just one catch on the year, which is nowhere near the breakout season managers were projecting. He'll likely be thrown to by Tyson Bagent against Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).

roster.name: Garrett Wilson
roster.outlook: Garrett Wilson's clear lead role in the Jets' passing game could pay dividends against a porous Lions secondary in Week 3. Wilson has registered seven targets in each of the Jets' first two outings, giving him ample opportunity to exploit a defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing wideouts through two weeks. The Lions' defense is vulnerable to all positions, but Wilson's spot as the top target is unchallenged.

roster.name: DJ Moore
roster.outlook: DJ Moore will need to overcome a shoulder injury if he is to help the Bills in Week 3 against the Chargers. After showing sound chemistry with Josh Allen in his first action for Buffalo, Moore failed to haul in a touchdown late in the second quarter in Week 2, suffering the injury that forced him to miss the second half. The Chargers have allowed three touchdowns to opposing receivers through two weeks and two 75-plus yardage performances, which should thrust Moore back into fantasy relevance if he's able to reprise his No. 1 WR role.

roster.name: Marvin Harrison Jr.
roster.outlook: Marvin Harrison will look to bounce back from his Week 2 goose egg when the Cardinals face San Francisco in Week 3. Harrison was targeted by QB Jacoby Brissett just once Sunday in a loss to the Seahawks and finished without a catch. The third-year receiver concerningly has just one catch for 33 yards through two weeks, and perhaps even more distressingly for his fantasy managers, he's drawn only four targets to Michael Wilson's 14 so far. The 49ers rank in the top 10 through two weeks by giving up only 247 receiving yards to wideouts.

roster.name: Rico Dowdle
roster.outlook: Rico Dowdle and the Steelers host the Bengals and their 14th-ranked run defense in Week 3. He finished Pittsburgh's loss last week with seven carries for 22 yards and caught both targets for 22 yards. Dowdle left the game in the second quarter with a toe injury, was cleared and returned to play in the second half but then left for good after appearing to re-injure the same toe. Keep an eye on his status in practice this week, as there's a good chance he'll be limited, thus leaving his status for Sunday's contest against the Bengals in question.

roster.name: Aaron Jones Sr.
roster.outlook: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions to arise with mobile quarterback Kyler Murray returning. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.

roster.name: Kenyon Sadiq
roster.outlook: Kenyon Sadiq could be poised for a major breakout for the Jets in Week 3 if Mason Taylor (thumb) is unable to play against the Lions. Sadiq has played just 42% and 38% of the offensive snaps through two games, easing into the rotation after recovering from hernia surgery prior to the year. The Jets' offense isn't prolific, but the matchup with a porous Lions' defense could change that. Detroit has allowed two touchdown catches to opposing tight ends in each of the first two weeks and 187 total yards, the second-highest total across the league.

roster.name: Trevor Lawrence
roster.outlook: Trevor Lawrence crashed back down to earth with 189 passing yards and no TDs in the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver after tossing four touchdown passes in the season-opening win over Cleveland. Lawrence and the Jaguars return home for a Week 3 showdown with the Patriots, who have allowed just 16 total points in two games. The daunting matchup drops Lawrence to the QB1/QB2 borderline, so this could be the week to plug in an alternative option if available. Lawrence threw 22 touchdown passes in the eight starts preceding his Week 2 dud, so the 2021 first-overall pick maintains elite upside.

roster.name: Eddy Pineiro
roster.outlook: Eddy Pineiro remains a solid fantasy kicker option heading into the 49ers' Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Pineiro didn't attempt a field goal Sunday against the Dolphins, but he converted all five of his extra-point tries. San Francisco has averaged 31.0 points per game through two weeks, so Pineiro figures to see frequent opportunities to kick, though that won't always result in field-goal chances. Arizona's opponents have attempted just one FG through two weeks, but the Cardinals gave up a hefty 31 points to Seattle in a Week 2 loss.

roster.name: Mike Washington Jr.
roster.outlook: Mike Washington hasn't seen much action to begin his NFL career, getting 10 carries through the Raiders' first two games and turning them into 48 yards. He also failed to bring in his only target. Ashton Jeanty is locked into the top spot in the backfield and has 54 touches, third in the league behind only Jahmyr Gibbs and Kenneth Walker, and unless he gets hurt, Washington's workload figures to be limited. The rookie will look to take advantage of the chances he does get in Week 3 against a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.

roster.name: Antonio Williams
roster.outlook: Antonio Williams snagged all three of his targets for 24 yards in the 37-20 loss to the Cowboys last game. Williams has seven catches for 98 yards and a touchdown through hsi first two NFL contests. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Williams and the rest of the Washington offense.

roster.name: Braelon Allen
roster.outlook: Braelon Allen's usage remains questionable as the Jets prepare to face the Lions in Week 3. After a run-heavy Week 1 where Allen had 10 attempts, that number was cut in half in Week 2. He has also only seen two targets through two games. Breece Hall remains the workhorse, and the Lions' vulnerability to chunk plays in the passing game could further phase Allen out of meaningful touches, despite Detroit allowing 5.2 yards per carry.

roster.name: Puka Nacua
roster.outlook: Puka Nacua (hip) is uncertain to play in the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Nacua missed Monday's Week 2 game versus the Giants, though he wasn't ruled out until game day. That lends some hope that Nacua could return soon, though his availability for practice during the week should provide more insight about his potential to return versus the Broncos. Should Nacua suit up, he'll draw a tough Denver secondary that have given up just 203 receiving yards to wideouts so far, tied for third-fewest in the league.

roster.name: Brock Bowers
roster.outlook: Brock Bowers is on track to make his season debut in Week 3 against the Saints after missing the Raiders' first two games due to minor knee surgery at the end of training camp. Knee trouble in 2025 prevented Bowers from repeating his dynamic rookie campaign, but if he's able to get fully healthy again, the star tight end should quickly emerge as the team's top option in the passing game, with little competition from a wide receiver room led by Tre Tucker. Bowers will initially be catching passes from Kirk Cousins, but at some point this season Las Vegas will transition to Fernando Mendoza under center, providing one more wrinkle for the offense. If he gets cleared this week as expected. Bowers will be facing a New Orleans defense that has yet to allow a touchdown to a TE in 2026.

roster.name: Carnell Tate
roster.outlook: Carnell Tate is off to an uninspiring start, with seven catches for 65 yards on 11 targets through two games with the Titans. A Week 3 road game against the injury-riddled Giants presents a nice opportunity for the rookie fourth overall pick out of Ohio State to break out, as the Giants just allowed 195 receiving yards and two TDs to Rams WR Davante Adams. Tate leads his team in targets through two games, but the Titans have struggled to move the ball through the air. Given Tate's draft pedigree and matchup, he's a high-ceiling fantasy WR3 for Week 3, though it's fair for fantasy managers to be hesitant given the highly touted rookie's lackluster production so far.

roster.name: Caleb Williams
roster.outlook: Caleb Williams is not expected to play in Week 3 as the Bears take on the Eagles. Williams went down with what looked like a freak injury against the Vikings in Week 2, but he now sits week-to-week with a hamstring ailment. Tyson Bagent is slated to get the start versus an Eagles offense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks across two games.

roster.name: Tony Pollard
roster.outlook: Tony Pollard could be worth plugging into Week 3 fantasy lineups as a high-end RB3/flex option for the Titans' road matchup with a Giants defense that has struggled to contain RBs in the early going. Javonte Williams scored two TDs against the Giants in Week 1, then Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each exceeded 90 scrimmage yards against the Giants in Week 2, with Williams tacking on a TD. Pollard has reprised his role as the 1A option in Tennessee's backfield over Tjyae Spears. The former Cowboys RB has averaged 77 scrimmage yards per game since joining the Titans prior to the 2024 campaign, but Pollard has been limited to 99 yards through two games to begin this season. Negative game scripts are often a problem for the Titans, but Tennessee is likely to stay within striking distance and keep Pollard involved on the ground against a Giants team that's missing starting QB Jaxson Dart (knee).

roster.name: Kyle Monangai
roster.outlook: Kyle Monangai should remain a high-volume RB2 as the Bears take on the Eagles in Week 3. Monangai saw double-digit carries once again in Week 2, but he totaled just 47 yards on the ground and tacked on 11 yards off two catches. The second-year running back has now seen 12 touches in each of Chicago's two outings this year, and he could see even more with Tyson Bagent slated to start under center. Philly has also ceded a top-ten 216 rushing yards to RBs this season.

roster.name: J.K. Dobbins
roster.outlook: J.K. Dobbins' workload has been limited to begin the season, with just 18 carries for 72 yards through the Broncos' first two games. The veteran back also has yet to see a target, as RJ Harvey and rookie Jonah Coleman have been prioritized as pass-catchers. Dobbins picked up a minor hamstring injury in Week 2's win over the Jaguars, but the issue isn't expected to keep him out of the lineup in Week 3. The same can't be said for Harvey, however, who didn't play at all in Week 2 due to his own hamstring strain. Dobbins could split touches with Coleman again in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

roster.name: Romeo Doubs
roster.outlook: Romeo Doubs will look to build on Week 2's uptick in workload in the Patriots offense when they face the Jaguars in Week 3. After not catching a pass in his Week 1 debut, Doubs snagged three of four targets for a team-high 96 yards in Week 2. New England's passing game is sputtering, and despite A.J. Brown missing the last game and a half, Doubs has not logged heavy volume. Jacksonville's secondary was just beaten for 138 yards by Jaylen Waddle, but otherwise, has held up with only one touchdown to opposing wideouts. Until his opportunities increase, Doubs presents a risky profile.

roster.name: Jalen McMillan
roster.outlook: Jalen McMillan will look to bounce back from a lackluster 2026 debut in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McMillan returned from a knee injury in the Week 2 loss against the Browns but played just seven offensive snaps. He'll likely be more involved as the season progresses, but with Tampa Bay's offensive struggles (five turnovers and two total touchdowns through two weeks), he may struggle to find fantasy relevance. Additionally, he's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that allowed just three points to the Bears in Week 2.

roster.name: Isiah Pacheco
roster.outlook: Isiah Pacheco will remain sidelined in Week 3 as the Lions take on the Jets. Pacheco was placed on IR to start the season due to a back injury, and he recently underwent surgery. This puts the former Kansas City RB's return in jeopardy as the season progresses. He's currently expected to be back sometime in December, so Sione Vaki will handle any RB2 duties behind Jahmyr Gibbs.

roster.name: Zachariah Branch
roster.outlook: Zachariah Branch is expected to play a depth role in Atlanta's WR room in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Branch played just 13 offensive snaps in the Week 2 loss to the Panthers -- which is five less than he logged in Week 1. It appears as if the rookie wideout's primary role is a return man, as he's operated as Atlanta's top punt returner this season. Branch's role could grow as the season progresses, but he's unlikely to find fantasy relevance in Week 3. Additionally, the Packers' defense has given up just 175 passing yards per game this season, making it an unfavorable matchup.

roster.name: Tyler Loop
roster.outlook: Tyler Loop and the Ravens visit the Cowboys for a Week 3 showdown. He finished 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and connected on both PATs during Baltimore's 24-17 loss in Week 2. Loop's first attempt from 49 yards was blocked, but he followed up by making his second attempt from the same distance. He should have plenty of opportunities to score in what's expected to be a high-scoring contest versus Dallas inside the AT&T Stadium dome in Week 3.

roster.name: Michael Mayer
roster.outlook: Michael Mayer hasn't made much of an impact as the Raiders' top tight end through the first two weeks of the season, catching nine of 11 targets for 55 yards without scoring a touchdown. That role has come while Brock Bowers was recovering from minor knee surgery at the end of training camp, but with Bowers expected to return in Week 3, Mayer will see even his modest volume collapse. If Bowers' 2026 debut does get delayed further, Mayer will still be facing a Saints defense that has yet to allow a TD to a tight end so far.

roster.name: Christian McCaffrey
roster.outlook: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.

roster.name: Chase Brown
roster.outlook: Chase Brown and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to battle their division rivals in Week 3. He tallied 20 carries for 80 yards and corralled three of five targets for two yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 win. Brown handled 23 of 26 touches out of the backfield, and he should continue to dominate those looks again in Week 3. The Steelers' defense ranks 26th in fantasy points allowed (27.5) to RBs after giving up 136 rushing yards and 4.9 yards per carry to the Patriots in Week 2.

roster.name: George Pickens
roster.outlook: George Pickens was second on the Cowboys in targets last game.  Pickens managed six catches for just 40 yards, though, as CeeDee Lamb went wild for Dallas. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Pickens has a disappointing nine catches for only 68 yards through two games for Dallas. The task may not get easier in Week 3, as Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

roster.name: Breece Hall
roster.outlook: Breece Hall will look to find more running room for the Jets in Week 3 against the Lions. He was limited to 1.8 yards per carry in Week 2, but 16 rushes was encouraging, as were his five catches on five targets. Detroit's defense is leaky, and while their secondary has been the more glaring weakness, they're allowing 5.2 yards per carry. The Jets' offensive limitations will likely temper Week 3 production, but Hall's workload in a plus matchup boosts his outlook.

roster.name: Davante Adams
roster.outlook: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).

roster.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
roster.outlook: Harold Fannin and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3 for their 2026 home opener. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with five catches on six targets for 54 yards. Fannin is still searching for his first TD of the season after collecting six as a rookie, as fellow tight end Blake Whiteheart was on the receiving end of a 17-yard score from Deshaun Watson. Fannin looks to find the end zone against Carolina's eighth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (9.0) to TEs.

roster.name: Mike Evans
roster.outlook: Mike Evans picked up a hip injury in San Francisco's win over Miami on Sunday, but early indications suggest he'll be fine for a Week 3 matchup versus the Cardinals. Evans has established a nice rapport with QB Brock Purdy so far this season, as the veteran wideout has caught nine of 10 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. San Francisco's WR corps has been thinned by the season-ending injury to rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson's more recent ankle injury, which will likely sideline him for Week 3, so Evans' availability as a reliable target for Purdy has taken on increased importance. Arizona was crushed by star wideout Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) in Week 2 and has given up four total receiving TDs to wideouts through two games.

roster.name: Makai Lemon
roster.outlook: Makai Lemon had just one catch in Philadelphia's win over Tennessee. Lemon is battling with Darius Cooper for the No. 3 wideout spot, as Dontayvion Wicks has all but claimed No. 2 for his own. Lemon had just one target last game, while Cooper had three and Wicks managed six. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.

roster.name: Dak Prescott
roster.outlook: Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns last game in a virtuoso performance for the Cowboys. Prescott completed 26-of-31 throws for 279 yards and the four scores in the dominant 37-20 win over the Commanders. Prescott has six touchdowns and just one pick through the first two games of the young season. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

roster.name: Kenny Gainwell
roster.outlook: Kenneth Gainwell is expected to play as the Buccaneers' No. 2 running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Gainwell was thought to be Tampa Bay's top receiving back heading into the season, but he's caught just three of four targets through two games, which is far less than Bucky Irving (11 receptions on 11 targets). Additionally, Gainwell has been relatively inefficient, averaging just 2.9 yards per touch. He's set to face one of the best defenses in the NFL in Minnesota, who have allowed just 3.4 yards per carry this season.

roster.name: Jordan Mason
roster.outlook: Jordan Mason will be out for Week 3 as the Vikings take on the Bears. Mason hurt his thumb after week one against the Packers, and he's been placed on IR for the injury. Mason will remain sidelined for at least the next three weeks, priming veteran Aaron Jones for a continued big role moving forward.

roster.name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
roster.outlook: Ka'imi Fairbairn had a rare miss on a difficult 58-yard field-goal attempt in Houston's Week 2 loss, but he remains one of the NFL's best kickers after leading the league in both made and attempted field goals last season. Fairbairn is locked in as a high-end fantasy starter for a Week 3 road game against a Colts team that has been the NFL's worst defensively. Indianapolis is allowing 37.0 points and 514.5 yards per game, both league highs.

roster.name: Kaelon Black
roster.outlook: Kaelon Black enters a Week 3 tilt against Arizona having established himself as San Francisco's clear No. 2 back. While Black has caught only one pass (on one target) through two contests, he's carried the ball 21 times -- one more than starter Christian McCaffrey (20 carries) and well ahead of No. 3 RB Jordan James (four totes). Of course, McCaffrey is the unquestioned leader of the 49ers' backfield, but Black has at least carved out a significant role and put himself on the fantasy radar in his first NFL campaign. The Cardinals just gave up 144 total rushing yards to Seattle's Jadarian Price and Emanuel Wilson in a loss Sunday, so they could be vulnerable against San Francisco's ground game.

roster.name: Adonai Mitchell
roster.outlook: Adonai Mitchell hopes for a continued elevated workload in Week 3 when the Jets face the Lions. After just three targets in a run-heavy Week 1, Mitchell logged an eye-opening 12 targets in Week 2, with the Jets throwing 41 times. Detroit's defense has been a fantasy bonanza for opposing offenses, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to wideouts. Assuming the Lions score plenty themselves, the Jets should throw heavily, giving Mitchell ample opportunities for a big play or two.

roster.name: Mike Gesicki
roster.outlook: Mike Gesicki and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh for an AFC North showdown in Week 3. After leading Cincinnati in receptions, yards, and targets in the season opener, Gesicki failed to record a single target versus the Texans in Week 2. Some of that could be chalked up to game flow with the Bengals ahead for most of the game, but it's nonetheless worrisome. The Steelers rank second in fantasy points allowed per game (5.5) and are first in receptions allowed to TEs through two weeks.

roster.name: Jaxon Smith-Njigba
roster.outlook: Jaxon Smith-Njigba enters Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington riding the wave of a three-touchdown performance. That effort came Sunday versus Arizona, when the star wideout also caught nine passes for 155 yards. Smith-Njigba worked with backup QB Drew Lock in that victory due to Sam Darnold being sidelined with a glute injury, and it seems that the reigning AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year is more than capable up dominating regardless of who is throwing him the ball. Smith-Njigba could be in for another huge effort against a Commanders defense that has surrendered the 10th-most receiving yards (337) to wideouts through two contests.

roster.name: Josh Jacobs
roster.outlook: Josh Jacobs is unlikely to play in the Packers' Week 3 matchup against the Falcons. Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List at this point in the season, with no current indications of when he'll be back in action. A committee of MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson will continue to be Green Bay's rushing attack with the veteran absent.

roster.name: Chris Olave
roster.outlook: Chris Olave is expected to remain one of fantasy's top receivers in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Olave ranks second in the NFL in both receptions (18) and receiving yards (268) through the first two weeks, cementing himself as New Orleans' top wideout. Currently, he's received a 25.6 percent target share, which should continue proving valuable with the Saints high-volume of pass attempts (90 through two weeks, second-most in the NFL). Olave could struggle against the Raiders, however, whose defense has allowed just 21.9 PPR fantasy points to wideouts per game this season.

roster.name: Bucky Irving
roster.outlook: Bucky Irving is expected to remain Tampa Bay's lead back in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Irving remained efficient despite the Buccaneers' offensive struggles in Week 2, accounting for 90 total yards on 21 touches. Additionally, he's operated as the clear No. 1 running back, out-touching Kenneth Gainwell 36 to 11 in two contests. Irving will likely struggle in Week 3, however, as he'll be facing a Vikings defense that's allowed just 14.7 PPR fantasy points to RBs this season, the fourth-best mark in the NFL.

roster.name: Luther Burden III
roster.outlook: Luther Burden will aim to get things going as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Burden has had a slow start to his sophomore campaign, with just eight catches on 12 targets for 95 yards across two games. He could also be in for even worse output, given the unknowns that come with Tyson Bagent set to start under center for Caleb Williams (hamstring). He'll take on a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.

roster.name: Courtland Sutton
roster.outlook: Courtland Sutton has had a slow start to the season as the focus of the Broncos' passing game has shifted to Jaylen Waddle. Through two games, Sutton has posted only nine targets, catching five for a meager 36 yards. He still has plenty of existing chemistry with quarterback Bo Nix, and the duo could rekindle it once defenses begin shifting more attention to Waddle, but Sutton figures to be hard-pressed to reach 1,000 receiving yards in 2026 for a third straight season. He'll take on a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, though three of them have gone for touchdowns.

roster.name: Matthew Golden
roster.outlook: Matthew Golden will remain a top option for Jordan Love as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Golden led Green Bay in receiving yards against the Jets in Week 2, catching four of six targets for 58 yards. The second-year wide receiver is also now set to take on more of a role, at least in the short term, with Jayden Reed looking to miss some time with a neck injury.  Golden will look to expand on his 10-153-0 receiving line against an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.

roster.name: Justin Herbert
roster.outlook: Justin Herbert has had a rough start to the season with Mike McDaniel as his new offensive coordinator. Through two games, he's completed less than 60% of his passes with a 2:3 TD:INT ratio and barely over 200 passing yards per game. Ladd McConkey was his only reliable target in the Chargers' opener, but the third-year wideout was limited by a rib injury in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and no one else stepped up. As in years past, Herbert's protection has also been decimated by injuries. An offensive line that was already missing starting center Tyler Biadasz was down to a third-string left guard against Las Vegas in Week 2, and the team also lost its two best blocking tight ends, Charlie Kolar and David Njoku, over the course of that contest. Herbert could be in for another long day in Week 3 against a Bills defense that has seven sacks through two games, tied for fourth in the league, but which has been vulnerable through the air when the opposing QB has found some time.

roster.name: Jonathon Brooks
roster.outlook: Jonathon Brooks (groin) is expected to operate as the Panthers' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Brooks is considered week-to-week after tweaking the same groin he first injured during training camp in the Week 2 win over the Falcons. Prior to his injury, the Texas product was clearly operating as Carolina's second RB, tallying just nine carries for 30 yards and two catches for 43 yards over the team's first two contests. Brooks will likely to find fantasy relevance if active in Week 3, with Cleveland's defense allowing just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game to the position thus far.

roster.name: Travis Kelce
roster.outlook: Travis Kelce continued a strong start to his 14th NFL season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 9-101-1 line on 11 targets. The future Hall of Famer last delivered a 1,000-yard campaign in 2022, but he's jumped out to an early pace in 2026 that would see him top 1,400 receiving yards and set a new career high. With Patrick Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Kelce may need to rely on spike games rather than steady production for his fantasy value. He'll take on a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's allowed 10.2 yards per target to tight ends through two weeks, 27th in the league.

roster.name: Bo Nix
roster.outlook: Bo Nix rebounded from a sluggish opener to lead the Broncos to a comeback win over the Jaguars in Week 2. The third-year QB has a meager 2:2 TD:INT through two games and has yet to add any production on the ground, but his 288 passing yards In Week 2 were more than double the Week 1 total, and his completion rate jumped from 60.7% to 71.0%. Nix also began establishing some chemistry with new top wideout Jaylen Waddle, who erupted for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets. Nix will face a Rams defense in Week 3 that has held opposition QBs under a 60% completion rate to begin the season.

roster.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
roster.outlook: Deebo Samuel is coming off a quiet game heading into San Francisco's Week 3 matchup against the Cardinals. Samuel caught three passes for 31 yards and rushed once for four yards in Sunday's rout of Miami. However, fellow wideouts Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both exited that contest due to injury, and though early reports suggest Evans should be fine for Week 3, Samuel could see more looks come his way given his comparatively good health. Arizona has given up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts so far this year and was just torched by Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba (9-155-3 receiving line) on Sunday.

roster.name: Tyler Shough
roster.outlook: Tyler Shough will lead the Saints' offense into a Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has allowed just 17.4 fantasy points per game to opposing quarterbacks this season. Shough has been one of the NFL's most productive QBs through two weeks, leading the league in passing yards (662) while producing five total touchdowns. Despite throwing the ball 90 times in his first two contests, Shough remains one of the league leaders in completion percentage (68.9 percent). He's in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, however, with the Raiders' allowing just one passing touchdowns this season.

roster.name: Cairo Santos
roster.outlook: Cairo Santos will aim to do more as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Santos made his first field-goal attempt against the Vikings in Week 2, but his second chance for a tie was blocked in the fourth quarter. The veteran kicker's potential for the rest of the season remains up in the air, but an inexperienced Tyson Bagent could get the field-goal team on the field more. Philly has allowed a bottom-ten 6.0 fantasy points per game to kickers this year.

roster.name: MarShawn Lloyd
roster.outlook: MarShawn Lloyd will aim to be more efficient as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Lloyd scored his first career touchdown off a six-yard catch in Week 2, but he also rushed six times for just 20 yards. The inexperienced running back has now averaged just three YPC off 19 carries this season, which is far from what Green Bay is looking for out of their RB1. Lloyd will also face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a bottom-ten 127 rushing yards to running backs, which could make his job even harder.

roster.name: Jahmyr Gibbs
roster.outlook: Jahmyr Gibbs will aim to keep things rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Gibbs finished with huge numbers once again in Week 2, but most of his output came from six catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. The superstar running back will make an effort to stay solid with such high volume, with 56 touches for 299 yards and three touchdowns to his name so far this season. He'll face a New York defense that's shelled running in their first two games, but they've faced no one of Gibbs' caliber.

roster.name: Tetairoa McMillan
roster.outlook: Tetairoa McMillan is expected to remain one of the Panthers' top targets in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. McMillan bounced back in Week 2 after a lackluster Week 1 performance, catching five of 10 targets for 101 yards while leading the team in receiving. The 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year is tied with Jalen Coker for the most targets on Carolina (18) entering Week 3, which is a positive sign for both players' outlooks going forward. With the Panthers' offensive success through two games, McMillan should be in for a great Week 3 matchup, especially while facing a Browns defense that's given up four receiving touchdowns to WRs through two contests.

roster.name: Rome Odunze
roster.outlook: Rome Odunze will look to remain a top look in Chicago's passing offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Odunze caught three of four targets for 43 yards against the Vikings in Week 2, and he now sits at a 5-95-0 receiving line across two games. The third-year pass catcher's unimpressive output could continue, given that Tyson Bagent is slotted to start under center in place of Caleb Williams (hamstring). Odunze will face a Philadelphia defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 29.4 PPR points per game to WRs this season.

roster.name: Lamar Jackson
roster.outlook: Lamar Jackson and the Ravens look to bounce back after a tough loss when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. Jackson threw for 235 yards (21-for-31) with one TD and one INT while rushing four times for 34 yards in Week 2's 24-17 loss. Baltimore draws a favorable matchup against a Dallas defense that ranks 27th in fantasy points allowed (27.2) and 31st in rushing yards allowed to QBs. Zay Flowers (hamstring) missed Week 2's contest, but the hope is that Jackson's speedy receiver makes it back on the field in Week 3.

roster.name: Chuba Hubbard
roster.outlook: Chuba Hubbard is expected to remain the Panthers' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Hubbard appears to have returned to his 2024 form over Carolina's first two games this season, rushing for 102 yards (4.6 yards per carry) and a touchdown while catching all five of his targets for 49 yards and a score. Additionally, with Jonathon Brooks (groin) exiting the Week 2 win in the fourth quarter, Hubbard's role could continue growing. He faces a difficult matchup, however, as the Browns' defense has given up just 16.9 PPR fantasy points per game through two weeks.

roster.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Thomas has notched exactly three catches for 40 yards in each of his first two games this season, providing a baseline expectation for the 2024 first-round pick's production in Jacksonville's Week 3 home game against the Patriots. Thomas is certainly capable of more, considering he averaged over 75 receiving yards per game as a rookie and scored 10 TDs that year, but has only two TDs in 16 games since then and is unlikely to score against a Patriots defense that has allowed only one touchdown this season. Perhaps breakout teammate Parker Washington will draw attention from top Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez to free up some space for Thomas to operate, but Thomas' lackluster production since the start of last season coupled with the tricky matchup make him a low-end flex play at best for Week 3.

roster.name: Jake Ferguson
roster.outlook: Jake Ferguson scored twice last game for the Cowboys. Ferguson caught four passes for 43 yards and the two scores in the 37-20 win over Washington. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL. In addition, the Ravens have given up just two passing touchdowns through two tilts.

roster.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
roster.outlook: Jacory Croskey-Merritt took 12 carries for 43 yards in Washington's loss to Dallas last game. Meanwhile, fellow running back Rachaad White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. Croskey-Merritt looks like the preferred back between the tackles, with White acting as the pass-catching or third-down option. The timeshare will likely continue against a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. In addition, Seattle has yet to allow a rushing touchdown to the opposition, and the Commanders will be without their starting quarterback, Jayden Daniels due to injury.

roster.name: Mark Andrews
roster.outlook: Mark Andrews and the Ravens look to rebound from an upset defeat when they visit the Cowboys in Week 3. He caught six of seven targets for 49 yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss, making it two straight outings with exactly 49 receiving yards for the 31-year-old. Andrews draws a favorable matchup versus a Dallas defense that surrendered eight receptions for 78 yards and two TDs to Isaiah Likely in the season opener. The Cowboys rank 26th in fantasy points allowed (16.9) and are one of two teams with a catch rate of 100% to TEs.

roster.name: Xavier Worthy
roster.outlook: Xavier Worthy scored his first touchdown of the season in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, snagging a one-yard toss from Patrick Mahomes in the second quarter. Worthy has notched steady target volume early in the season, with 13 total looks, but that has resulted in just an 8-43-1 line, and he has yet to get a carry. With Mahomes spreading the ball around and the offense prioritizing Kenneth Walker and the run game, Worthy will need some big plays to make a real fantasy contribution. The third-year speedster will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.

roster.name: Harrison Mevis
roster.outlook: Harrison Mevis is still searching for his first field-goal conversion heading into the Rams' Week 3 clash against Denver. Mevis didn't try a FG in Week 1, and he missed his only attempt -- a 43-yarder -- on Monday Night Football. Mevis did make all four of his extra-point tries and figures to kick a lot of those given the Rams' explosive offense. Kickers have gone 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts against the Broncos so far this season.

roster.name: Jonah Coleman
roster.outlook: Jonah Coleman didn't see the ball in his NFL debut during the Broncos' opener, but his role increased in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to RJ Harvey's hamstring strain. Coleman ended up getting more touches than J.K. Dobbins, with the 2026 fourth-round pick turning 10 carries into 39 yards and his first career touchdown while also catching all three of his targets for 19 yards. It's not clear how much time Harvey might miss, but Coleman's solid showing in his first opportunity could begin the process of turning the backfield into a three-man committee, with the workload dependent on whoever happens to be healthy. Coleman could be a risky play in Week 3 against a Rams defense that just saw the return of Aaron Donald in Week 2 and has yet to allow a rushing TD this year.

roster.name: Bryce Young
roster.outlook: Bryce Young will look to stay hot in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns, whose defense has surrendered 22.1 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Young has been one of the most productive QBs in the NFL through two weeks, as he's tied for the most touchdown passes in the league (six) while ranking second in passing yards (648). He's also threatened defenses with his legs, adding 16 yards and a score on the ground. Young could very well finish as one of fantasy's top quarterbacks again in Week 3 while playing a Browns defense that's allowed five touchdown passes this season.

roster.name: Chris Bell
roster.outlook: Chris Bell will look for a breakout opportunity in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has drawn only three targets through two weeks, resulting in one catch and a declining snap share, playing just 40% of offensive plays last week. A potential absence from Caleb Douglas (ankle) could elevate Bell to a WR2 role in a struggling offense that often throws while playing from behind. Kansas City's pass defense has been stingy, but should Douglas sit, Bell would be an intriguing high-upside option if chasing points in Week 3.

roster.name: Jonathan Taylor
roster.outlook: Jonathan Taylor has scored multiple rushing TDs in both of the Colts' games heading into a Week 3 home tilt against the Texans. The star RB led the NFL with 20 scrimmage TDs last season and looks poised to finish near the top of the leaderboard again this season. Taylor is a set-and-forget fantasy RB1, even against a stout Texans front seven that allowed the fourth-fewest rushing yards to RBs last season and has yet to allow a TD to the position.

roster.name: Trey McBride
roster.outlook: Trey McBride remains one of the most matchup-proof pass catchers in the league heading into the Cardinals' Week 3 tilt versus San Francisco. Though QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards in a loss to Seattle on Sunday, McBride accounted for 41 of those yards and got into the end zone. Through two weeks, McBride leads NFL tight ends with 17 receptions and ranks fourth with 136 receiving yards. The 49ers have been tough on the position so far, though, giving up just seven catches for 52 yards.

roster.name: DeVonta Smith
roster.outlook: DeVonta Smith broke loose last game for the Eagles, snagging 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Titans. Smith saw a team-best 13 targets for the game, a pace which should continue in the absence of A.J. Brown. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury.

roster.name: Javonte Williams
roster.outlook: Javonte Williams was rather quiet last game for Dallas. Williams managed just 50 yards from scrimmage and did not find the end zone versus Washington, as the passing game took the spotlight in the 37-20 win. Williams may also have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL. However, Baltimore has allowed three rushing touchdowns already, which is tied for 23rd in the league.

roster.name: Bhayshul Tuten
roster.outlook: Bhayshul Tuten emerged as the clear No. 1 option in Jacksonville's backfield heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, ahead of Chris Rodriguez and pass-catching specialists LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah. Through the first two games of his sophomore season, Tuten turned 28 carries and three targets into 150 scrimmage yards and one TD. The speedster is a viable RB3/flex for Week 3, though expectations should be tempered against a New England defense that's off to an elite start, having allowed just 16 points through two games.

roster.name: Matthew Stafford
roster.outlook: Matthew Stafford will look to replicate a huge Week 2 performance when the Rams face Denver in Week 3. On Monday Night Football, Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception against the Giants. The reigning NFL MVP didn't have star wideout Puka Nacua (hip) for that contest, so he turned to veteran Davante Adams, who logged eight catches for 195 yards and two of Stafford's TDs. Denver could pose a more potent threat, as the Broncos have a talented secondary and have limited QBs to a 74.5 passer rating, fifth-best in the NFL, through two weeks.

roster.name: Parker Washington
roster.outlook: Parker Washington has established himself as the No. 1 WR for the Jaguars and is headed toward weekly fantasy WR1 territory ahead of a Week 3 home game against the Patriots. New England has one of the league's best secondaries, led by CB Christian Gonzalez, but Washington appears largely matchup-proof considering the 24-year-old WR just accounted for 98 of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards in a Week 2 loss to Denver that could wind up being Lawrence's worst performance of the season. Washington has at least five catches and 83 receiving yards in each of his last five games, as well as three touchdown catches over that span, so the breakout star can be started with confidence regardless of the opponent.

roster.name: Jaylen Warren
roster.outlook: Jaylen Warren and the Steelers welcome the Bengals to town for a Week 3 AFC North matchup. He rushed 11 times for 43 yards and brought in two of four targets for 34 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Warren handled 11 of 20 carries from backs in this one, but the Steelers weren't able to get much going on offense. It looks like he's the 1A out of the backfield, and although it's not by a substantial amount, Rico Dowdle is considered questionable to suit up on Sunday with a toe injury. Warren faces a 14th-ranked Cincinnati defense in fantasy points allowed (19.0) to RBs.

roster.name: Brandon Aubrey
roster.outlook: Brandon Aubrey connected on all three of his field goals last game for Dallas, including a 60-yarder. Aubrey also booted four extra points, shaking off a surprising miss in Week 1 versus the Giants. In Week 3, the Cowboys clash with the Ravens. Baltimore is allowing 23.5 points per tilt, which is in the middle of the pack so far in 2026.

roster.name: Jayden Reed
roster.outlook: Jayden Reed's status is up in the air as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Reed was carted off the field after injuring his back on the first drive of Week 2, which in itself makes it unlikely that he'll be rushed back for a TNF matchup. The fourth-year playmaker's absence would give Matthew Golden even more looks, with Skyy Moore and Bo Melton slotting in as supplementary options for Jordan Love. If Reed somehow does play, he'll face an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.

roster.name: Jalen Coker
roster.outlook: Jalen Coker is expected to remain one of Bryce Young's favorite targets in Carolina's Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Coker has been incredibly productive, leading the Panthers in receptions (16) and yards (204) while being tied for first in targets (18) through two weeks. Across his last three games (including playoffs), the third-year pro has caught 25 of 30 targets for 338 yards and two touchdowns, emerging as one of the NFL's top young wideouts. He's in for a very favorable matchup in Week 3 as well, as the Browns' defense has surrendered 7.2 yards per pass attempt this season.

roster.name: Juwan Johnson
roster.outlook: Juwan Johnson is expected to remain one of New Orleans' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite a dip in snap rate and route share compared to Week 1, Johnson paced the Saints' tight end corps in receptions, targets and yards in Week 2. He ranks third on the team in targets and yards, which is a positive outlook for his value going forward. However, Johnson is in for an unfavorable matchup, as Las Vegas' defense has allowed just 10.3 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

roster.name: Malik Willis
roster.outlook: Malik Willis figures to labor again in Week 3 when the Dolphins host the Chiefs. He has yet to top 220 yards or complete more than 15 passes through two games, and his rushing attempts haven't been as plentiful as anticipated. Any potential late production while playing from behind has also failed to manifest, and that game script figures to repeat in Week 3 against Kansas City, a defense that's allowed only 341 passing yards, two touchdown passes, and 12 rushing yards this season.

roster.name: Rashod Bateman
roster.outlook: Rashod Bateman and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 3 matchup against the Cowboys. In the absence of top wideout Zay Flowers (hamstring), Bateman caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and a touchdown during Baltimore's Week 2 loss. He'll likely slide back to a supporting role if Flowers is able to suit up this Sunday. However, if he's unable to do so, Bateman will have the chance to replicate his solid outing versus a Dallas defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) allowed to WRs.

roster.name: CeeDee Lamb
roster.outlook: CeeDee Lamb went wild last game for the Cowboys. Lamb caught eight passes for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the win over Washington. Lamb had nine targets for the game. He has scored three touchdowns in his first two contests of the 2026 campaign. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

roster.name: Kenneth Walker III
roster.outlook: Kenneth Walker has had a dazzling start to his Kansas City tenure, topping 100 rushing yards in each of his first two games and piling up 369 scrimmage yards in total with two touchdowns, one rushing and one receiving. The former Seahawk is thriving in a bell cow role, and his 6.2 yards per carry would be a career high if he can keep it up. Walker will take aim in Week 3 at a Dolphins defense that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.

roster.name: Travis Etienne Jr.
roster.outlook: Travis Etienne is expected operate as New Orleans' top running back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Despite signing a big contract with the Saints this past offseason, Etienne saw just 10 opportunities in the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He still leads the team in carries (17) but saw less work through the air, with Alvin Kamara (five catches on six targets) returning to the lineup. With Kamara back, Etienne may struggle to be fantasy relevant without finding the end zone against a Raiders defense that's allowed just 17.5 PPR fantasy points per game to RBs this season.

roster.name: Jaylen Waddle
roster.outlook: Jaylen Waddle broke out in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, erupting for an 8-138-0 line on 10 targets as he began to get on the same page as quarterback Bo Nix. Waddle logged plenty of downfield targets but also had a red zone look, usage that promises plenty more big performances. The former Dolphin hasn't had a 1,000-yard season since 2023, but the early returns in Denver suggest he'll have little trouble returning to that level in 2026. He'll face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of those have gone for touchdowns.

roster.name: Terry McLaurin
roster.outlook: Terry McLaurin led the Commanders in targets last game with nine opportunities. Unfortunately, Scary Terry could only cash in two of those chances for 50 yards in a loss to the Cowboys. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for McLaurin and the rest of the Washington offense.

roster.name: Jayden Daniels
roster.outlook: Jayden Daniels dislocated his elbow against the Cowboys in Week 2, the same elbow he injured last year for the Commanders. While the elbow is not fractured, Daniels is almost certain to miss Week 3 vs. the Seahawks. Veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start versus a devastating Seattle defense that is allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt.

roster.name: Christian Watson
roster.outlook: Christian Watson remains the top option in Green Bay's offense as they take on the Falcons in Week 3. Watson finished with a quieter four catches for 41 yards and a touchdown against the Jets in Week 2, but he did garner an impressive 11 targets. The fifth-year wideout has now scored three touchdowns on a team-high 19 targets across two games. He'll take on an Atlanta defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 30.3 PPR points per game to WRs.

roster.name: Michael Pittman Jr.
roster.outlook: Michael Pittman and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. After dealing with a foot injury during training camp and the preseason, he suffered a new foot ailment that forced him to miss Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss in New England. Pittman will have to practice in some capacity in order to return for Sunday's contest, but it sounds like his status for Week 3 is very much in question. Consider him doubtful to suit up until we hear otherwise.

roster.name: Brock Purdy
roster.outlook: Brock Purdy will look to build upon a historic performance when San Francisco faces Arizona in Week 3. Purdy completed 20 of 22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns with no turnovers against Miami on Sunday, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That stat line made Purdy the second passer in NFL history with 250 passing yards on a 90 performance completion rate in multiple games. The fifth-year signal caller may be without some of his weapons in Week 3 if Mike Evans (hip) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) need to sit out, though early reports suggest Evans isn't dealing with a serious injury. The Cardinals could have a hard time containing Purdy after giving up 235 passing yards and three TDs to Seattle QB Drew Lock in a Week 2 loss.

roster.name: Dallas Goedert
roster.outlook: Dallas Goedert suffered a knee injury last game for Philadelphia and did not return, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus Chicago. Goedert is set to undergo testing to determine the nature and extent of the issue. Johnny Mundt caught two apsses in Goedert's place, and would be the next man up if Goedert cannot suit up. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.

roster.name: Quentin Johnston
roster.outlook: Quentin Johnston has struggled through the Chargers' first two games, catching just three of 11 targets for 24 yards. The fourth-year wideout had emerged as a deep option over the prior two seasons, but new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme is built on quick passes and yards after the catch, giving little time for Johnston's typical downfield routes to develop. Tre' Harris and rookie speedster Brenan Thompson both seem better suited to that style of passing game, and Johnston runs a real risk of becoming an afterthought as the season progresses. He does at least get a potentially favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.

roster.name: George Holani
roster.outlook: George Holani may be asked to take on a bigger offensive role for Seattle in a Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. Jadarian Price suffered a shoulder injury late in a Week 2 win against Arizona, and if he isn't able to suit up versus Washington, Holani would figure to see more work, though Emanuel Wilson would presumably take over No. 1 RB duties. As it is, Holani has gotten involved on offense in each of Seattle's contests so far, combining to produce 42 yards on 12 carries and two yards on one reception. The Commanders have been decimated through the air this season, but they haven't surrendered a rushing touchdown so far.

roster.name: Harrison Butker
roster.outlook: Harrison Butker missed a 51-yard field-goal attempt in the second quarter of Week 2, but he made up for it by converting the rest of his opportunities, including a 40-yard FG that gave Kansas City the overtime win over the Colts. The veteran kicker has been busy in the early going with six FG attempts and seven PATs, and a resurgent offense led by a healthy Patrick Mahomes and new bell-cow back Kenneth Walker should continue to supply Butker with volume. He'll face a Dolphins team in Week 3 that's giving up 31.0 points a game in the early going.

roster.name: Terrance Ferguson
roster.outlook: Terrance Ferguson is coming off a big game as the Rams prepare to face Denver in Week 3. Ferguson notched six catches on nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown on Monday Night Football, trailing only star wideout Davante Adams in receptions, targets and receiving yards. That followed Ferguson's quiet Week 1 performance, when he didn't catch his only target. Repeating Monday's big effort could be tough for Ferguson in Week 3, as he'll face a Broncos defense that limited Jacksonville's tight ends to a modest 24 receiving yards Sunday.

roster.name: Emmett Johnson
roster.outlook: Emmett Johnson logged only four touches as Kenneth Walker's primary backup in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, as the fifth-round rookie continues to get his feet wet in the NFL. Johnson also saw a little work as a kickoff returner as the team looks to find ways to get the ball in his hands. As long as Walker is healthy, Johnson's workload will remain limited, but he's flashed some big-play potential in the early going with 64 receiving yards on just four catches. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's been more vulnerable through the air than on the ground so far in 2026, allowing 3.5 yards per carry, which ranks sixth in the league.

roster.name: De'Von Achane
roster.outlook: De'Von Achane's volume remains elite as the Dolphins get set to host the Chiefs in Week 3. Achane has amassed 31 carries and 11 targets through two weeks, and while his 3.5 yards per carry is modest, there aren't many other options with such a safe workload. Kansas City is allowing 4.0 yards per carry, and they'll surely stack the box against Achane, as everyone else is doing. However, the Chiefs have allowed four catches to an opposing back in consecutive weeks. Achane's volume generates a floor, with scoring providing upside.

roster.name: Ashton Jeanty
roster.outlook: Ashton Jeanty has looked the part of a bell-cow running back to begin his second NFL season, amassing 54 touches through two games and turning them into 210 scrimmage yards and two receiving touchdowns. The 2025 first-round pick is still only averaging 3.4 yards per carry however, and the Raiders' offseason upgrades to the offensive line haven't yet led to better efficiency on the ground for Jeanty. He'll try to take advantage of a Week 3 clash with a Saints defense that ranks in the bottom four in rushing yards and rushing TDs allowed to RBs so far in 2026.

roster.name: Zay Flowers
roster.outlook: Zay Flowers and the Ravens are in Dallas for a Week 3 matchup between 1-1 teams. He was ruled out of Baltimore's Week 2 loss with a hamstring injury he suffered in the season opener, so his status in practice this week will be something to monitor. If he's able to suit up in Week 3, Flowers will face a Cowboys defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points per game (31.2) and 13th in receiving yards allowed to WRs. In his absence, Rashod Bateman put up a 7-88-1 receiving line on nine targets as Lamar Jackson's No. 1 receiver.

roster.name: Tee Higgins
roster.outlook: Tee Higgins and the Bengals are in Pittsburgh to take on their division rivals in Week 3. He finished Week 2's win over Houston with five catches on 10 targets for 95 yards, pacing Cincinnati in yardage and targets. Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase accounted for 19 of Joe Burrow's 31 pass attempts, and that's likely to remain the case despite an unfavorable Week 3 matchup. The Steelers' defense ranks second in fantasy points allowed per game (15.5) and has yet to surrender a TD to WRs in 2026.

roster.name: TreVeyon Henderson
roster.outlook: TreVeyon Henderson will look to build on an impressive debut when New England faces Jacksonville in Week 3. After missing Week 1 due to an ankle injury, Henderson shouldered 16 carries in Week 2, putting up 76 yards and a touchdown. While he wasn't targeted in the passing game, Henderson showed his elite big-play ability. Rhamondre Stevenson was an afterthought after losing an early fumble, but with New England struggling to pass the ball effectively, this has the look of a run-first, split backfield. Jacksonville is allowing just 3.2 yards per carry and 110 total rushing yards through two weeks, which will keep Henderson's Week 3 expectations in check.

roster.name: Joe Burrow
roster.outlook: Joe Burrow and the Bengals are on the road to face the Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with back spasms in practice, Burrow was a full go in Week 2, throwing for 207 yards (20-for-31) with two TDs and no INTs in the 20-6 victory. He faces a stout Pittsburgh defense that ranks first in fantasy points allowed (11.6) to QBs and seventh in passing yards allowed. Burrow is one of the best at his position, but fantasy managers should approach this matchup with caution after the Steelers held Drake Maye to 208 passing yards (14-for-22) with one pick while sacking him three times in Week 2.

roster.name: Michael Wilson
roster.outlook: Michael Wilson faces a tough challenge in Arizona's Week 3 matchup in San Francisco. Wilson was quiet against Seattle this past Sunday, catching just two of seven targets for 18 yards. However, he was still the Cardinals' second-leading receiver in a game during which QB Jacoby Brissett threw for just 95 yards. The 49ers have surrendered only 15.6 fantasy points per game to wideouts, the ninth-best mark in the league threw two weeks.

roster.name: RJ Harvey
roster.outlook: RJ Harvey wasn't able to suit up in Week 2's win over the Jaguars due to a hamstring strain, putting his availability for a Week 3 matchup against the Rams in question. The second-year back was expected to be the pass-catching complement to J.K. Dobbins for the Broncos, but rookie Jonah Coleman handled that role and didn't look out of place. If Harvey misses too much time, Coleman could take his job, but Dobbins' own checkered injury history could leave Denver patching together a backfield from whoever is healthy.

roster.name: Khalil Shakir
roster.outlook: Khalil Shakir remains a steady, stable cog in Buffalo's passing game entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Shakir logged six targets in each of the Bills' first two games but hasn't topped 50 yards or scored. Shakir didn't take on an elevated role in Week 2 following DJ Moore's (shoulder) early exit, but he faces a secondary that allowed 75 yards to Kendrick Bourne and 119 yards to Tre Tucker, and both operate in a similar slot role to Shakir.

roster.name: Jerry Jeudy
roster.outlook: Jerry Jeudy and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3, whose defense allowed just 145 yards through the air in Week 2. He failed to corral his lone target during Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2, giving him a 2-26-0 receiving line on five targets through two games. Meanwhile, rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion combined for 123 yards and one TD while catching 11 of 13 targets, and they look to be the leaders in the WR room. It will be difficult to start any of them until the Browns' offense consistently proves it can sustain any fantasy-relevant players.

roster.name: Travis Hunter
roster.outlook: Travis Hunter didn't have a target or carry in Week 2 and has played only a handful of snaps on offense for the Jaguars this season. He's off the fantasy radar heading into a Week 3 home game against the Patriots, outside of IDP formats that reward Hunter's contributions as a cornerback. Parker Washington, Brian Thomas, and Jakobi Meyers should continue to lead Jacksonville's wide receiver room.

roster.name: Jake Bates
roster.outlook: Jake Bates will seek to stay perfect as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. Bates has now drilled both of his two field-goal attempts and all eight of his XPAs this season. The third-year kicker hasn't been on the field for many field goals this season, and Detroit playing from behind doesn't help his case. Luckily, the current high volume of touchdowns has kept Bates relevant. He'll face a New York squad that's allowed a bottom-ten 6.0 points per game to kickers across two games.

roster.name: Kayshon Boutte
roster.outlook: Kayshon Boutte had three catches in his second game with the Texans in Week 2 after going without a catch in his team debut. He's probably the best downfield option in the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring), who looks likely to sit out again in Week 3 against the Colts after missing the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati. The Colts have talent in their secondary, led by CB Sauce Gardner, but they are vulnerable to big plays through the air since they often leave their cornerbacks in one-on-one coverage with receivers. Indianapolis has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL this season, so Boutte has starter-level upside in deep leagues for Week 3.

roster.name: C.J. Stroud
roster.outlook: C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but led the Texans to just six points in the absence of top WR Nico Collins (hamstring) during Week 2's loss to the Bengals. If Houston remains without Collins in Week 3 against the Colts, Stroud will likely lean heavily on TE Dalton Schultz once more against a Colts defense that allowed 41 points to the Ravens and then 33 to the Chiefs. Considering the Colts have surrendered the most points and yards in the NFL, Stroud is worth a look in superflex or multi-QB lineups, but he will likely remain ranked outside the starting range in single-QB formats, at least until Collins returns.

roster.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
roster.outlook: Amon-Ra St. Brown will aim to stay hot as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. St. Brown finished with a monster performance in Week 2, bringing in nine of 13 targets for 142 yards and two touchdowns. Not only has the star pass catcher recorded back-to-back two-TD performances, but he's also now amassed 19 catches for 209 yards in that stretch. He should continue to benefit from Detroit's shaky defense, even against a New York defense that's allowed a bottom-10 (27.2) PPR points per game to their first two opponents.

roster.name: Rashee Rice
roster.outlook: Rashee Rice's volume ticked up in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, posting a 4-83-0 line on six targets. Xavier Worthy has been getting more looks from Patrick Mahomes, and Rice's targets have mainly come very close to the line of scrimmage. He's got the run-after-catch ability to turn those short receptions into big gains, but he may not be a high-volume option in an offense that has prioritized Kenneth Walker and the running game. Rice will face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.

roster.name: Kyren Williams
roster.outlook: Kyren Williams will look to get into the end zone for the Rams again in Week 3 versus Denver. Williams posted a 12-85-0 rushing line against the Giants on Monday Night Football and added a 2-12-1 line through the air. The veteran running back has scored each of the first two weeks of the campaign after racking up double-digit scores each of the past three seasons. The Broncos have struggled against the run so far in 2026, allowing the third-most rushing yards (286) to running backs.

roster.name: Ladd McConkey
roster.outlook: Ladd McConkey was clearly limited by a rib injury in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, catching all three of his targets for 35 yards. That was still good enough to tie for the team lead in receptions, however, as Justin Herbert and the entire offense continue to adjust to the new scheme instituted by OC Mike McDaniel. McConkey is Herbert's clear top downfield option, and as he gets healthier, his production should begin to look more like the 5-82-1 line he delivered in the season opener before getting hurt in the third quarter. McConkey will get a favorable matchup in Week 3 against a Bills secondary that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.

roster.name: David Montgomery
roster.outlook: David Montgomery produced just 24 scrimmage yards in Houston's Week 2 loss to the Bengals after scoring three TDs in his Texans debut. The veteran RB will cede some backfield work to Woody Marks, particularly if the Texans are forced to play catch-up, but Montgomery is the team's preferred option in valuable red-zone and short-yardage situations. Montgomery is poised for a bounce-back effort in Week 3 and can be trusted as a fantasy RB2 against a Colts defense that's allowing 177 yards per game on the ground.

roster.name: Patrick Mahomes
roster.outlook: Patrick Mahomes has Kansas City's offense humming, and through two games, he's produced 566 passing yards and a 5:1 TD:INT while adding a touchdown on the ground. The superstar QB has spread the ball around effectively, as five different targets have been on the end of those TDs, and a revitalized running game with Kenneth Walker has prevented defenses from laying back and clogging the passing lanes. Mahomes could be headed for big numbers in Week 3 against a Dolphins defense that has yet to record a sack in 2026 and which sits 32nd in completion rate against at a stunning 78.8%.

roster.name: Tucker Kraft
roster.outlook: Tucker Kraft will look to get more involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Kraft was held to just two catches for 15 yards in Week 2, but Green Bay's passing attack was lacking for most of the game. The bruising tight end will seek to re-establish himself as a top outlet for quarterback Jordan Love moving forward. Luckily, an Atlanta defense that's allowed the fourth-most 20.7 PPR points per game to tight ends so far this season could be a great place to start.

roster.name: Josh Downs
roster.outlook: Josh Downs is poised to work as the Colts' top wide receiver in Week 3 against the Texans, making him a solid WR3 or flex option in fantasy. Alec Pierce (heel) is expected to sit out, and the Colts lack viable alternatives, with over-the-hill veteran Keenan Allen and recent signing Darius Slayton representing the top options behind Downs in the wide receiver room. Downs caught seven of nine targets for 72 yards to lead the Colts in all three categories during the Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, which Pierce exited in the first half. Downs figures to see plenty of star Texans CB Derek Stingley, but the 25-year-old WR should get plenty of targets from Daniel Jones despite the tricky matchup.

roster.name: Woody Marks
roster.outlook: Woody Marks capitalized on a negative game flow in Week 2, out-touching David Montgomery 13-8. The 0-2 Texans will face a Colts team that's also 0-2 in Week 3, and Montgomery is likely to reclaim the lead role unless Houston falls into a multi-score hole again. Marks is averaging just 2.9 yards per carry and 4.2 yards per catch in 2026 after averaging a modest 3.6 yards per carry during his 2025 rookie season. He has RB3/flex upside in Week 3 against a Colts defense that's giving up 177 rushing yards per game, but Marks' uncertain role and poor efficiency this season cap his value despite the intriguing matchup.

roster.name: Chris Godwin Jr.
roster.outlook: Chris Godwin will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Buccaneers' Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Godwin leads Tampa Bay's receiving corps in offensive snaps played (101) and has caught all seven of his targets through two weeks. However, this hasn't translated to much production, as he's accumulated just 86 receiving yards. Expect Godwin to remain one of the Buccaneers' most reliable targets in a difficult matchup against a Vikings defense that's given up just 27 receptions to wideouts through two games.

roster.name: Alvin Kamara
roster.outlook: Alvin Kamara is expected to operate as the Saints' top pass-catching back in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. In his return from a sprained MCL in the Week 2 win over the Ravens, Kamara led the Saints' backfield in carries (nine), targets (six) and receptions (five). Despite this, Travis Etienne was more efficient with his opportunities, averaging 3.1 yards per carry compared to Kamara's 1.7. Even so, the Saints' backfield is in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that's allowed just 3.8 yards per carry thus far.

roster.name: Cam Little
roster.outlook: Cam Little had a rare miss in Week 2 but has been one of the NFL's best kickers since entering the league in 2024. Through 36 games with the Jaguars, he has converted 61 of 68 field-goal attempts, including an NFL-record 68-yard field goal. He's a little riskier than usual in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing just 8.0 points per game, but Little is probably too good to bench regardless of the opponent.

roster.name: Tyler Allgeier
roster.outlook: Tyler Allgeier will seek to improve his efficiency on the ground during Arizona's Week 3 visit to San Francisco. Allgeier gained just 10 yards on five carries Sunday in a loss against Seattle, and he's averaging a meager 3.2 YPC through two contests. He paced the Cardinals with 17 carries in the team's season opener, but  Jeremiyah Love jumped ahead with him with nine carries Week 2 and could continue to settle in as the club's clear No. 1 RB moving forward. The 49ers have yielded 4.04 YPC to running backs so far, but that's led to just one rushing TD.

roster.name: Devaughn Vele
roster.outlook: Devaughn Vele is expected to remain the Saints' No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Raiders, whose defense has given up just 15 receptions to WRs through two contests. Vele has clearly positioned himself as one of New Orleans' top receiving options early in the season, catching 12 of 16 targets for 133 yards and one touchdown thus far. He's expected to continue benefitting from the Saints' high volume of pass attempts, as Tyler Shough has already thrown the ball 90 times in two games, the second-most in the NFL. Despite this, Vele is in for a difficult Week 3 matchup against a Las Vegas defense that has yet to allow a receiving touchdown this season.

roster.name: Chris Brooks
roster.outlook: Chris Brooks should continue to stay involved as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Brooks was a non-factor on the ground against the Jets in Week 2 (four carries for 11 yards), but he did reel in his first catch of the season for 15 yards. The fourth-year running back should remain on the field for passing-situation plays moving forward, especially since he served that role last season even with Josh Jacobs on the field. He'll face an Atlanta defense that's been rigid on RBs so far this season, allowing a bottom-ten 16.3 PPR points per game.

roster.name: Justin Jefferson
roster.outlook: Justin Jefferson will look to build off a quieter week as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jefferson was held to three catches for 55 yards against the Bears in Week 2, but the game had bad weather and ended with a 9-3 score. The superstar pass catcher has 11 catches for 147 yards and two touchdowns this season, and he could increase those numbers twofold against a Bucs defense that ceded 95 yards and a touchdown to Cleveland receiver Denzel Boston this past Sunday.

roster.name: Saquon Barkley
roster.outlook: Saquon Barkley missed portions of Philadelphia's last game due to a stinger, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Saquon had five carries for just 20 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown, while Will Shipley saw nine touches and managed 29 yards overall. Bigsby and Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

roster.name: Josh Allen
roster.outlook: Josh Allen has the Bills offense firing on all cylinders heading into a Week 3 matchup with a slumping Chargers squad. Allen has thrown for five touchdowns and run in four in a dominating start to his 2026 season. The Chargers are a desperate team, but they'll also be traveling across the country and have been victimized by far less capable quarterbacks in Jacoby Brissett (277 yards, one TD) and Kirk Cousins (253/3), suggesting the elements are there for Allen to continue his elite production.

roster.name: Quinshon Judkins
roster.outlook: Quinshon Judkins and the Browns welcome the Panthers to town for an interconference showdown in Week 3. He finished Cleveland's 23-19 upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with 12 carries for 21 yards and caught all five targets for 27 yards. No other running back tallied more than two carries, so it's clear Judkins is still the No. 1 option out of the backfield, but that hasn't come with much success through two weeks of action. Next up is a Carolina defense that ranks 31st in fantasy points allowed (36.3) and last in TDs surrendered to RBs.

roster.name: Jameson Williams
roster.outlook: Jameson Williams will look to do more as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3.
