Williams' output has been disappointing so far this season, with just six catches for 78 yards across two games. The fifth-year wideout has also reaped no benefits from Detroit's struggling defense, with Amon-Ra St. Brown currently carving out a monopoly in the wide receiver room. Williams will face a New York defense that's allowed a bottom-10 (27.2) PPR points per game to their first two opponents.

roster.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
roster.outlook: Kyle Pitts will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Pitts has really struggled along with the majority of Atlanta's offense throughout the first two weeks, catching just one of four targets for 15 yards. However, he could really benefit from the return of Michael Penix as the team's starting quarterback heading into Week 3. While Penix was healthy during the 2025 season, Pitts averaged 4.2 receptions and 41.7 yards per game -- a vast difference from his 2026 production thus far. He's also in for a favorable matchup, as the Packers' defense has allowed 12.0 PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

roster.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
roster.outlook: Rhamondre Stevenson's opportunities are questionable as the Patriots prepare for the Jaguars in Week 3. After a 23-touch season debut, Stevenson lost a fumble early in Week 2, an issue that's plagued him throughout his career, and ended with just seven touches. In a split backfield with Treveyon Henderson, New England will likely ride the Week 3 hot hand. Facing a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing rusher to go over 39 yards, both backs could be running uphill.

roster.name: Sam LaPorta
roster.outlook: Sam LaPorta will look to remain a top target as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. LaPorta recorded six catches for 52 yards and his first touchdown of the season against the Bills in Week 2. The starting tight end has now been targeted 15 times across two games, and he's converted these into 11 grabs for 100 yards and a touchdown. He'll face a New York defense that held Green Bay's Tucker Kraft to just two catches for 15 yards this past Sunday.

roster.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
roster.outlook: Wan'Dale Robinson is off to a slow start with the Titans, but he'll try to recapture his magic from last season with the Giants when he faces the Giants in Week 3. The shifty WR was peppered with short targets during his last couple seasons with the Giants, racking up 140 targets apiece in 2024 and 2025. After exceeding 1,000 receiving yards in 2025, Robinson signed a four-year, $78 million contract to join former Giants head coach and current Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll in Tennessee. Robinson is on pace for just 60 targets with his new team, so his involvement is likely to grow moving forward. It will be tough to trust Robinson until Tennessee's passing game shows some signs of life, but there is some deep-league fantasy flex appeal here for Week 3, especially in PPR formats, against a banged-up Giants secondary.

roster.name: Denzel Boston
roster.outlook: Denzel Boston and the Browns host the Panthers in a Week 3 clash between 1-1 teams. The rookie followed up his 2-59-1 receiving line in the opener with an even better outing against the Buccaneers, tallying five catches on seven targets for 95 yards and another TD. Boston led the team in yardage and targets, as he's quickly becoming Deshaun Watson's preferred target, particularly downfield. He faces a vulnerable Carolina defense that ranks 18th in fantasy points allowed (30.3) to WRs.

roster.name: Tank Bigsby
roster.outlook: Tank Bigsby had 15 touches and a touchdown in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Bigsby and Will Shipley would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge. The Eagles will face a Bears run defense in Week 3 allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

roster.name: Kyler Murray
roster.outlook: Kyler Murray will return to the field as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Murray has cleared concussion protocol after suffering a nasty hit early in Week 1. The veteran quarterback will finally get the chance to prove himself, especially given that he completed just three of five passes for 18 yards and one interception before his opening-game departure. He'll face a Bucs defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 20.4 fantasy points per game to QBs across their first two games.

roster.name: Chris Boswell
roster.outlook: Chris Boswell and the Steelers host the Bengals in Week 3. The 12th-year kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to New England. Both of Boswell's attempts came from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 1-for-3 from that distance and 3-for-5 overall through two outings in 2026. He'll look to get back on track this Sunday versus a Cincinnati defense allowing 16.5 points per game, tied for eighth.

roster.name: Stefon Diggs
roster.outlook: Stefon Diggs has scored three times in two games as a member of the Commanders. Diggs snagged five passes for 47 yards and two touchdowns in Washington's loss to Dallas last week. Unfortunately, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, so veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Diggs and the rest of the Washington offense, though the newly acquired wideout does seem to have a knack for finding the end zone thus far in 2026.

roster.name: Caleb Douglas
roster.outlook: Caleb Douglas' status for the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs is uncertain due to an ankle injury. Douglas played a hefty 85% of the team's offensive snaps before suffering the injury late in Week 2 but recorded just 19 yards after a 94-yard career debut. Should he play, Douglas is a speculative upside play for fantasy teams in need of Week 3 help.

roster.name: James Cook III
roster.outlook: James Cook faces a challenge for fantasy managers in the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. Cook and Buffalo's offense motored through Detroit last week, their lead back finishing with 139 total yards and a touchdown. The Chargers have been stingy against the run, allowing a mere 2.98 yards per carry to the likes of Ashton Jeanty and Jeremiah Love. Teams beat them through the air with far greater ease. Cook's role in this potent offense is unquestioned, but tempered expectations in Week 3 appear prudent.

roster.name: Omarion Hampton
roster.outlook: Omarion Hampton has been one of the few Chargers who seems to be benefiting from new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel's scheme. The second-year back racked up 115 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 2's loss to the Raiders, and he's been the clear top option in the backfield, getting 37 touches through two weeks compared to Keaton Mitchell's 10 and Kimani Vidal's zero. Hampton lost a fumble in each game, and that split could begin to shift Mitchell's way if ball security is deemed an issue for the 2025 first-round pick. Hampton could cash in on his bell-cow role in Week 3 against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.

roster.name: Jeremiyah Love
roster.outlook: Jeremiyah Love is still looking for his first big breakout game heading into Arizona's Week 3 clash in San Francisco. Love has notched 20 rushes for 70 yards and touchdown through two games while adding 25 yards on five catches. Meanwhile, Tyler Allgeier has posted a 22-71-0 line, as both RBs have struggled with efficiency in the early going. Love seems likely to eventually separate as the Cardinals' clear-cut top RB, though the veteran Allgeier could cut into his carries throughout the campaign. The 49ers have been impressive in getting off to a 2-0 start, though they're giving up 4.04 YPC to running backs, just 20th in the league so far.

roster.name: Emeka Egbuka
roster.outlook: Emeka Egbuka is expected to remain the Buccaneers' top receiving option in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings, whose defense has given up 38.9 PPR fantasy points to WRs this season. Egbuka had a rough Week 2 outing, finishing third on Tampa Bay in receptions (three) and targets (five) while slotting in at fifth in yards (16). However, he did score a touchdown and was on the field for 85 percent of the Buccaneers' offensive snaps, suggesting he'll remain the team's WR1. He's set for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Minnesota defense that gave up just three points and 163 passing yards to the Bears in Week 2.

roster.name: Jadarian Price
roster.outlook: Jadarian Price injured his shoulder in the Seahawks' Week 2 win over Arizona, and it's unclear if he'll be able to play in Week 3 against Washington. The rookie RB was injured in the fourth quarter versus the Cardinals and finished the game with 13 carries for 52 yards and one catch for eight yards. Should Price not be able to play in Week 3, Emanuel Wilson would be he lead candidate to take over as the Seahawks starting RB. The Commanders have been awful against the pass but decent against the run this season and are yielding just 3.79 YPC against running backs.

roster.name: Drake Maye
roster.outlook: Drake Maye will look to get on track when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. He is averaging just 183 passing yards through two weeks, with only one touchdown pass and four interceptions. Maye was picked off just eight times all last season. Opponents seem to be pressuring Maye, though Jacksonville is middling at getting after the passer. However, they've allowed only two touchdown passes while limiting quarterbacks to 44 rushing yards. With A.J. Brown still sidelined, Maye will be challenged to exhibit his 2025 form.

roster.name: Alec Pierce
roster.outlook: Alec Pierce aggravated a left heel injury in Week 2, stemming from his offseason left ankle surgery. The Colts' leading receiver from last season probably faces a multi-week absence and won't play against the Texans in Week 3. Josh Downs and Keenan Allen are set to lead Indianapolis' underwhelming WR room versus Houston.

roster.name: George Kittle
roster.outlook: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.

roster.name: Blake Corum
roster.outlook: Blake Corum should continue to be a big part of the Rams' backfield versus the Broncos in Week 3. Against the Giants on Monday Night Football, Corum racked up 79 yards on 12 carries while adding a 13-yard reception. Through two weeks, Corum has 22 carries to Kyren Williams'  23, so the pair appear to be headed for a pretty even workload in 2026. Denver could be vulnerable to both ball carriers, as the Broncos have given up a whopping 5.40 YPC to RBs this season -- third worst in the league.

roster.name: Cameron Dicker
roster.outlook: Cameron Dicker has had a rough start to the season as the Chargers adjust to a new offensive scheme under Mike McDaniel. The fifth-year kicker has converted all four of his PATs through two games, but his only field-goal attempt so far came from 58 yards out, and he clanked it off the upright. Better days should be ahead for Dicker and the offense, but his streak of seasons with 40-plus FG attempts could be about to come to an abrupt end. Dicker could be a little busier in Week 3 against a Bills team that's allowed 31.0 points a game in the early going, tied for the third-worst total in the league.

roster.name: KC Concepcion
roster.outlook: KC Concepcion and the Browns return home in Week 3 to host the Panthers and their 18th-ranked passing defense. He finished Cleveland's upset win over the Buccaneers in Week 2 with six catches on six targets for 28 yards and had one rush for minus-6 yards. Concepcion led the team in receptions but was last in average yards per touch at just 4.7. His general involvement on offense is a great sign, but it appears fellow rookie Denzel Boston is the Browns receiver to roster thanks to his big-play ability.

roster.name: Baker Mayfield
roster.outlook: Baker Mayfield is set for a difficult Week 3 matchup when the Buccaneers take on the Vikings, whose defense has allowed 20.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season. Mayfield has really struggled during Tampa Bay's first two contests, accounting for just two touchdowns while turning the ball over four times. He's thrown for just 184.5 passing yards per game while completing 71 percent of his passes. Additionally, he's in for a tough Week 3 matchup, with Minnesota's defense giving up just 12.5 points per game this season.

roster.name: Brenton Strange
roster.outlook: Brenton Strange was a non-factor during the Jaguars' Week 2 loss at Denver, but that was the case for every member of Jacksonville's passing game except for Parker Washington, who accounted for more than half of Trevor Lawrence's 189 passing yards. It won't be easy for Strange to bounce back in Week 3 against the Patriots, who are allowing just 8.0 points per game and have limited TEs to seven catches for 52 yards this season. There are likely better Week 3 options.

roster.name: Keenan Allen
roster.outlook: Keenan Allen should get plenty of playing time in Week 3 against the Texans with the Colts' banged-up WR room, but the 34-year-old wideout may not have enough gas in the tank to make much of the opportunity. Allen has exceeded 44 yards just once and failed to score a TD in his last 12 games. Despite that lack of recent production, he's a viable deep-league dart throw, as Indianapolis will be without Alec Pierce (heel) and possibly Ashton Dulin (ankle), leaving Allen as the top option for snaps at WR alongside Josh Downs.

roster.name: Bijan Robinson
roster.outlook: Bijan Robinson is expected to lead the Falcons' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has given up 22.9 PPR fantasy points per game to running backs this season. Despite Atlanta's offensive struggles through two weeks, Robinson has continued to produce, having recorded 254 total yards and a touchdown on 48 touches. With Michael Penix back at the helm for the Week 3 contest, Robinson should be in for even more production. Additionally, he's in for a favorable matchup, as Green Bay's defense has allowed three rushing touchdowns in its first two games.

roster.name: Drake London
roster.outlook: Drake London will look to bounce back from a slow start in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. London has caught just six of nine targets for 80 yards in Atlanta's first two games, as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand struggled to get the offense going. However, Michael Penix is set to return as the Falcons' QB1 during the Week 3 contest, giving London a far more optimistic projection. He's in for a favorable matchup as well, with Green Bay's defense allowing three receiving touchdowns and 34.5 PPR fantasy points per game to WRs this season.

roster.name: Nico Collins
roster.outlook: Nico Collins (hamstring) didn't suit up for the Texans in Week 2 and may not be ready to return against the Colts in Week 3. If Collins recovers, he'll jump back in as the top option in Houston's passing game and a fantasy WR2 at worst. Should Collins sit again, TE Dalton Schultz could continue to work as the primary pass catcher for C.J. Stroud, while the Texans get by with Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Jared Wayne at WR.

roster.name: Tyler Warren
roster.outlook: Tyler Warren has started his second NFL season on a two-game TD streak but has a meager 34 receiving yards on 12 targets. The Colts' 2025 first-round pick is poised to keep logging plenty of targets in Week 3 against the Texans, as Indianapolis is running out of NFL-caliber pass catchers in the absence of Alec Pierce (heel). Warren had six catches in the Week 2 loss to Kansas City, a game Pierce exited early. Given Warren's mix of talent and usage, he remains a top-10 fantasy TE in Week 3 against Houston's talented defense.

roster.name: D'Andre Swift
roster.outlook: D'Andre Swift will be a top option in Chicago's offense in Week 3 against the Eagles. Swift cooled down in Week 2 after a monster opener, logging 16 rushes for 45 yards on the ground. The veteran RB did see success in the passing game, logging five catches for 54 yards. With Tyson Bagent expected to start at quarterback for the Bears, Swift could be utilized more heavily on the ground. Philadelphia has also allowed a top-ten 216 rushing yards to running backs this season.

roster.name: Jalen Hurts
roster.outlook: Jalen Hurts tossed two touchdowns and two interceptions in a last-second win over Tennessee last game. Hurts threw for 264 yards in the rollercoaster battle and was able to overcome the two picks to find Darius Cooper for the winning score. Hurts has five touchdowns in two games for the Eagles. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL.

roster.name: DK Metcalf
roster.outlook: DK Metcalf and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional clash. He caught four of a team-high nine targets for just 27 yards during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Metcalf finished fifth in yardage despite tying Germie Bernard and Pat Freiermuth for second in receptions, and he now has an 8-67-0 receiving line on 19 targets through two outings. Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense have been underwhelming to begin the season, and they'll face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs.

roster.name: Rachaad White
roster.outlook: Rachaad White recorded 13 touches for 83 yards out of the backfield last game for the Commanders. White took seven carries for 43 yards, while also catching six passes for 40 yards as a receiver with Washington playing from behind. White remains in a timeshare for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt, though, and will face a devastating Seattle defense in Week 3.  The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points and 214 yards per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league in both categories.

roster.name: Jordan Addison
roster.outlook: Jordan Addison will seek to ramp things up as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Addison bounced back from a zero-catch performance in Week 1 this past Sunday, logging two catches for 21 yards against the Bears. Still, his output is nowhere near sufficient for fantasy owners, especially since he's put up WR2 numbers many times throughout the last three seasons. He'll face a Bucs defense that's ranked top 10 (24.9 PPR points per game) against wide receivers this season.

roster.name: Dalton Kincaid
roster.outlook: Dalton Kincaid brings momentum into the Bills' Week 3 matchup with the Chargers. After a 130-yard opener, Kincaid posted seven catches for 95 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 against Detroit, playing on 66% of the offensive snaps. Opportunity, not talent, has been an issue as he hasn't played over a 50% snap share since Week 5 in 2025. The Chargers were dominated by Tre McBride in Week 1 but rebounded against the Brock Bowers-less Raiders tight end room last week. Kincaid's big numbers are poised to continue in Week 3.

roster.name: Jakobi Meyers
roster.outlook: Jakobi Meyers has been targeted just three times through Jacksonville's first two games. That lack of volume makes him hard to trust as anything more than a deep-league dart throw in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that held the Seahawks and Steelers to a combined 16 points. Parker Washington (18 targets), Brian Thomas (11 targets), and even TE Brenton Strange (five targets) have all been higher on Trevor Lawrence's priority list than Meyers. To the veteran wide receiver's credit, Meyers's 28-yard effort on one target in the Week 2 loss to Denver marked the first time in 11 games as a member of the Jaguars that he failed to record at least 39 receiving yards. Therefore, he could rebuild a solid fantasy floor if Lawrence starts looking Meyers's way more frequently.

roster.name: Brian Robinson Jr.
roster.outlook: Brian Robinson (ankle) will operate as the Falcons' No. 2 running back if active for the Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Robinson logged 13 touches in Atlanta's Week 2 loss to the Panthers, but eight of those came in the fourth quarter -- suggesting he's still firmly the second option at RB. The Alabama product has been efficient, however, averaging 4.1 yards per carry through two weeks. He's also in for a favorable matchup, with the Packers defense allowing 22.9 PPR fantasy per game to RBs this season.

roster.name: Jason Myers
roster.outlook: Jason Myers has provided Seattle with a steady boot this season heading into a Week 3 matchup against Washington. The veteran kicker has made all three of his field-goal tries and all five of his PAT attempts through two weeks. However, he hasn't yet been asked to hit from distance, as none of his FG tries have been from 40 yards or greater. The Commanders have yielded a whopping 30.5 points per game through two weeks, so Myers could get plenty of opportunities to kick in Week 3.

roster.name: Cam Ward
roster.outlook: Cam Ward will be tough to trust outside of deeper multi-QB formats in Week 3, when the Titans face the Giants on the road. The 2025 first overall pick scored two short rushing TDs in Tennessee's surprisingly competitive Week 2 loss to the Eagles, matching his career total in that category heading into that game. Ward has just one touchdown pass this season and 16 touchdown passes through 19 NFL starts, of which he has won three. The Giants allowed two touchdown passes to Dak Prescott and four to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford, but those two veteran QBs are far more effective passers than Ward at this stage in their respective careers.

roster.name: T.J. Hockenson
roster.outlook: T.J. Hockenson will look to stay involved as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Hockenson saw his volume go down a bit in Week 2 against the Bears, reeling in just three catches for 29 yards. The starting tight end looks like he'll be a touchdown-dependent option moving forward. With that being said, Kyler Murray is slotted to start Sunday, and he's been known to rely on tight end options in the past. The Bucs have allowed a second-most 22.1 PPR points per game to TEs so far this season.

free_agents.name: Jared Goff
free_agents.outlook: Jared Goff will look to keep his high production rolling as the Lions take on the Jets in Week 3. Goff benefited from playing behind in Week 2 at Buffalo, racking up 327 passing yards and four touchdowns on a 68 completion rate. The veteran quarterback has now totaled 533 passing yards with a 6:0 TD:INT across his first two games, and Detroit's lacking defense has only helped his output so far. Goff will take on a New York defense that's allowed a bottom-10 fantasy points per game (14.2) to quarterbacks in the first two games of the season.

free_agents.name: Hunter Henry
free_agents.outlook: Hunter Henry will look to keep expanding his role for the Patriots in Week 3 against the Jaguars. In their first full game without A.J. Brown in Week 2, Henry logged a 92% snap share but drew only five targets, turning them into three catches for 40 yards. Drake Maye has struggled to open the season, posting a 1:4 TD:INT ratio, and while someone has to catch the limited passes, Henry faces a challenging matchup against a defense that hasn't allowed an opposing tight end to top 32 yards against them so far.

free_agents.name: Tyjae Spears
free_agents.outlook: Tyjae Spears is likely to see a handful of touches as usual for the Titans behind Tony Pollard in Week 3, but that projected usage is enough for Spears to earn flex consideration in deeper formats against a Giants defense that has struggled to defend RBs. The Giants just allowed at least 92 scrimmage yards apiece to the Rams' backfield duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, but the Rams boast one of the league's most talented offenses and led the league with 30.5 points per game last season, while the Titans are averaging 15.0 PPG after scoring 16.7 PPG last season. Spears can make big plays happen in space, as he showed in compiling 70 yards on nine touches in last week's loss to the Eagles, though he had just 24 yards on five touches in the season-opening loss to the Jets.

free_agents.name: Jordan Love
free_agents.outlook: Jordan Love will look to make a statement as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Love snuck out a win for Green Bay in Week 2, but a 55 completion rate for 145 yards, even with a 2:0 TD:INT ratio, was uninspiring against the Jets. The sixth-year gun slinger luckily still sits at 532 passing yards on the year with four touchdowns and one interception, and his high volume only looks to continue with Josh Jacobs' return remaining weary. He'll face an Atlanta defense that gave up 287 passing yards and three touchdowns to Bryce Young this past Sunday.

free_agents.name: Rashid Shaheed
free_agents.outlook: Rashid Shaheed enters Seattle's Week 3 game against Washington on the heels of a quiet but versatile start to the season. Shaheed logged a modest three catches for 35 yards against Arizona in a Week 2 win, though he promisingly ranked second on the Seahawks with six targets, added a four-yard rush and combined for 76 yards on three punt returns and two kickoff returns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba appears set to dominate Seattle's targets for a second straight campaign, so both Shaheed and Cooper Kupp may have to settle for complementary roles on offense. Nonetheless, Seattle's WR corps as a whole could thrive in Week 3 against a Washington defense that has yielded a 73.0 percent catch rate to the position, tied for fifth-highest in the league.

free_agents.name: Will Reichard
free_agents.outlook: Will Reichard will look to stay hot as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Reichard converted all three of his field-goal attempts in a close win over the Bears with tough conditions in Week 2. The third-year kicker has now nailed four field goals and all four of his XPAs this year. He'll face a Bucs squad that's tied for the most fantasy points per game allowed to kickers (13) so far this year.

free_agents.name: Evan McPherson
free_agents.outlook: Evan McPherson and the Bengals visit the Steelers for an AFC North divisional matchup in Week 3. He remained perfect on the season after connecting on both of his field-goal attempts and both PATs during Cincinnati's Week 2 win over Houston. McPherson drilled both of his field goals from 50-plus yards out, and he's now 6-for-6 on the season, with four of his makes coming beyond 50 yards. He'll continue to earn plenty of scoring opportunities on an elite offense, even despite Pittsburgh's strong defense.

free_agents.name: Daniel Jones
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Jones is averaging 188 passing yards per game heading into the Colts' Week 3 home game against the Texans. Houston gave up two touchdown passes apiece to star QBs Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, but Jones will be hard-pressed to post his first multi-TD performance of the season considering the Texans boast one of the league's best defenses, having allowed the fewest yards in the NFL last season. The Colts will continue to rely primarily on the legs of star RB Jonathan Taylor, and Indianapolis has an underwhelming group of pass catchers that's expected to be without last season's leading receiver Alec Pierce (heel) for several weeks. Jones has been a non-factor as a rusher since returning from a torn Achilles, with just 14 rushing yards this season. His mediocre passing stats make him an unappealing Week 3 fantasy option, even in multi-QB formats.

free_agents.name: Dontayvion Wicks
free_agents.outlook: Dontayvion Wicks continues to cement himself as the No. 2 wideout in the Eagles offense. Wicks caught five passes for 74 yards in the 24-20 win over the Titans. Wicks was second on the team in targets for the game. In Week 3, Philadelphia will face a Bears defense allowing 240 passing yards per tilt thus far this season, which is 25th in the NFL. The Eagles could also rely even more on the passing game if Saquon Barkley is sidelined due to injury, and with Dallas Goedert also banged up, Wicks could be one of the chief beneficiaries.

free_agents.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Chris Rodriguez has notched just six rushing attempts in each of his first two games with the Jaguars. He's averaging a paltry 3.0 yards per carry and has yet to earn a target in the passing game, where Rodriguez has been a non-factor his entire NFL career. Bhayshul Tuten has 28 carries this season and is the clear lead back for the Jaguars. Rodriguez isn't an advisable fantasy play in Week 3 against a Patriots defense that's allowing a minuscule 8.0 points per game.

free_agents.name: Tre Tucker
free_agents.outlook: Tre Tucker produced his first ceiling game of 2026 in the Raiders' Week 2 win over the Chargers. churning out a 5-119-1 line on seven targets. The volatile wideout is showing some early chemistry with new quarterback Kirk Cousins, and no one else has yet shown any indication that they'll be able to challenge him for the top spot on the depth chart, even if Tucker's skill set would be better suited for a WR2 or even WR3 role. Tucker will try to build on last week's effort in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

free_agents.name: Dalton Schultz
free_agents.outlook: Dalton Schultz paced the Texans with 12 catches for 140 yards on 14 targets in the Week 2 loss to Cincinnati, working as C.J. Stroud's top target in the absence of WR Nico Collins (hamstring). The veteran TE is the favorite to lead the team in targets if Collins sits in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most yards and TDs in the NFL this season. Indianapolis just allowed nine catches for 101 yards and a TD to Chiefs TE Travis Kelce in Week 2. Schultz is locked in as a fantasy TE1 for Week 3 if Collins sits and has a strong argument to stay in that range even if Collins suits up.

free_agents.name: Pat Freiermuth
free_agents.outlook: Pat Freiermuth and the Steelers play host to the Bengals for an AFC North clash in Week 3. He paced the team's tight ends in snaps (46), receptions (4), yards (32) and targets (5) during Pittsburgh's 20-3 loss to the Patriots. Freiermuth appears to have the upper hand over Darnell Washington (1-7-0) in the passing game, but his fantasy floor and ceiling are relatively low in an underwhelming Steelers offense. He'll have the added benefit of facing a Cincinnati defense that allows 18.5 fantasy points per game to TEs (27th) and just got torched for 12 receptions and 140 yards by Dalton Schultz.

free_agents.name: Sam Darnold
free_agents.outlook: Sam Darnold has a chance to return from a glute injury for Seattle's Week 3 matchup against the Commanders. It remains to be seen if the veteran QB will be able to suit up, but he reportedly has been ahead of schedule in his recovery. With Darnold out against Arizona in Week 2, Drew Lock took over and led the Seahawks to a win. Whichever signal-caller starts under center in Week 3 could feast upon a Washington defense that has allowed a 137.0 passer rating this season, the worst mark in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Chase McLaughlin
free_agents.outlook: Chase McLaughlin could remain one of the top kickers in fantasy despite the Buccaneers' tough Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. McLaughlin remained perfect in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, as he's now converted on all six field-goal tries this season, including two from 50-plus yards. Despite McLaughlin being tied for the league-lead in field-goals made this season, he could struggle against a Minnesota defense that's allowed just 6.5 kicking points per game thus far.

free_agents.name: Keaton Mitchell
free_agents.outlook: Keaton Mitchell has taken a clear backseat to Omarion Hampton in the Chargers' backfield to begin the season, getting 10 touches to his teammate's 37 through two games. Mitchell has yet to do much to earn a larger role, averaging just 3.7 yards per carry, although he does have a 15-yard gain on his only catch. Hampton has lost a fumble in each game so far in 2026, and these ball security issues could open the door for Mitchell to get more involved. If he does see more volume in Week 3, Mitchell could hit paydirt against a Bills defense that's allowed four touchdowns to RBs so far, two on the ground and two through the air.

free_agents.name: Calvin Ridley
free_agents.outlook: Calvin Ridley has drawn just two targets through two games in Tennessee's underwhelming passing game. The Titans don't have a player with more than 80 receiving yards heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, so Ridley's fantasy value is slim to none as a depth piece behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson. The Giants have struggled to defend WRs, but Ridley is unlikely to get enough passes thrown his way to capitalize on facing the banged-up Giants secondary.

free_agents.name: Justice Hill
free_agents.outlook: Justice Hill and the Ravens travel to face a Cowboys defense in Week 3 that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) allowed to running backs. He tallied two carries for six yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Baltimore's 24-17 Week 2 loss to the Saints. As long as Derrick Henry, who accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, is healthy, Hill's action will be limited as the No. 2 RB. However, in a contest that is expected to be high-scoring, Hill could contribute as a receiver, but he's still a risky fantasy play outside of deeper leagues.

free_agents.name: Trey Smack
free_agents.outlook: Trey Smack will aim to stay perfect as the Packers play the Falcons in Week 3. Smack went perfect in Week 2 against the Jets, nailing two XPAs and two field-goal tries, including a game-winner. The rookie boot has now gone a perfect five-for-five on field goals and made all but one of his four extra-point attempts. He'll take on an Atlanta team that's allowed a top-ten 9.0 fantasy points per game to kickers on the year.

free_agents.name: Cooper Kupp
free_agents.outlook: Cooper Kupp has so far had a quiet campaign heading into Seattle's Week 3 matchup versus Washington. Kupp has logged just two receptions in each of the Seahawks' first two games, registering 55 yards across the four total catches. He ranks third on the team with five targets, trailing Jaxon Smith-Njigba (22) and Rashid Sheheed (nine). As those numbers suggest, Smith-Njigba is dominating looks again this season, so Kupp and Shaheed may be left to compete for scraps throughout the campaign. With that said, there may be lots of receptions to go around against the Commanders, who have given up 27 catches to wideouts through two weeks -- tied for third-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Samaje Perine
free_agents.outlook: Samaje Perine and the Bengals travel to take on the division-rival Steelers in Week 3. After dealing with an illness that forced him to miss two days of practice, he was active in Week 2 and recorded two carries for six yards and caught his lone target for 16 yards during Cincinnati's win over the Texans. With backfield mate Chase Brown handling 23 total touches, Perine's limited involvement on offense makes him a solid fantasy insurance policy, but nothing more. Pittsburgh's defense ranks 28th in rushing yards (233) and 29th in receiving yards allowed (97) to RBs.

free_agents.name: Jalen Nailor
free_agents.outlook: Jalen Nailor has had a quiet start to his Raiders' tenure, catching four of eight targets for 36 yards through two games without a touchdown. He hasn't been able to get on the same page as quarterback Kirk Cousins, even though the two were together in Minnesota for the first two years of Nailor's career, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Nailor seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

free_agents.name: Kalif Raymond
free_agents.outlook: Kalif Raymond will look to stay involved as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Raymond was a consistent option once again in Week 2 against the Vikings, catching all five of his targets for 40 yards. The veteran wide receiver has now recorded 13 catches for 124 yards on 14 targets through two games. With quarterback Tyson Bagent also slated to get the start under center, Raymond could be a safe target against a middle-of-the-pack Philly defense against WRs (29.4 PPR points per game).

free_agents.name: Tyler Bass
free_agents.outlook: Tyler Bass will attempt to bounce back from his first miss of the season when the Bills host the Chargers in Week 3. Bass wasn't afforded a field goal try in Week 2, with Buffalo's offense finding the end zone with ease, but still provided a reasonable floor, hitting five of six extra points. The Bills' offensive efficiency could cap Bass' scoring potential, but historically, the highest-scoring kickers come from the highest-scoring teams.

free_agents.name: Jake Elliott
free_agents.outlook: Jake Elliott nailed a 58-yard field goal in Philadelphia's last game. Elliott has not missed a kick through two games for the Eagles, connecting on two field goals and six PATs. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears squad allowing 23 points per contest, which is in the middle of the pack thus far this NFL season.

free_agents.name: Ray Davis
free_agents.outlook: Ray Davis has limited involvement in Buffalo's offense entering Week 3 against the Chargers. Through two weeks, Davis has logged one carry and no targets as James Cook's primary backup, making his only contribution on kick returns. Facing a defense that's allowing just 2.98 yards per carry and with no clear path to an uptick in opportunities, Davis is an insurance policy for Cook managers only.

free_agents.name: Carson Wentz
free_agents.outlook: Carson Wentz will return to Minnesota's backup role in Week 3 against the Buccaneers. Wentz performed well while leading the Vikings to a 2-0 record, completing 23 of 39 passes for 276 yards and three touchdowns in that stretch. The veteran quarterback will remain a solid backup behind Kyler Murray, although anything can happen as the season progresses.

free_agents.name: Malik Washington
free_agents.outlook: Malik Washington brings steady volume ahead of the Dolphins' Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. With Malik Willis under center, Miami has completed just 29 passes through two games, but seven have gone to Washington, who's averaging 6.5 targets. Kansas City's rebuilt secondary has been terrific through two games, allowing just 204 yards to opposing wideouts. Washington seems unlikely to produce any massive numbers, but he also appears to be a steady cog in this limited offense, keeping him on WR3/Flex radars.

free_agents.name: Mack Hollins
free_agents.outlook: Mack Hollins will seek a bounce back performance in Week 3 when the Patriots face the Jaguars. After a solid four catch, 51-yard opener with A.J. Brown leaving early, Hollins notched only two targets in Week 2. New England's passing game is struggling with Drake Maye completing just 14 passes in Week 2. Until he begins to bounce back, trusting any of his pass catchers appears a risky proposition even against a defense that is allowing a generous 10.3 yards per target.

free_agents.name: Jaylin Noel
free_agents.outlook: Jaylin Noel could see extra opportunities in Week 3 if Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) misses a second consecutive game against the Colts. Noel has just three catches this season, but two of them have exceeded 30 yards. The 2025 third-round pick's big-play ability makes him a viable deep-league option in Week 3 against a Colts defense that has allowed the most points and yards in the NFL through two games. Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte, and Jared Wayne are the other healthy options in Houston's WR room.

free_agents.name: Aaron Rodgers
free_agents.outlook: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers host the division-rival Bengals in Week 3. He threw for 187 yards (23-for-39) with no touchdowns and one INT and lost one of his two fumbles during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Cincinnati has been somewhat stingy against opposing QBs, allowing 20.2 fantasy points through two outings (15th) despite giving up 353 passing yards versus Houston in Week 2. The Bengals are the only defense without an interception to this point, but they're also the only team that has yet to surrender a passing TD.

free_agents.name: Evan Engram
free_agents.outlook: Evan Engram had a minimal role in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars, catching his only target for 17 yards. The veteran tight end has notched just six targets through two games, and while he did get into the end zone in the season opener, the reduced volume he saw in 2025, his first year in Denver, doesn't look like it will improve in 2026. Engram will take on a Rams defense in Week 3 that's allowed just 64 receiving yards to TEs so far, sixth in the league, and has yet to allow one to score a touchdown.

free_agents.name: Jauan Jennings
free_agents.outlook: Jauan Jennings will hopefully return to action as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jennings sat out in Week 2 due to personal reasons, so his practice availability this upcoming week should dictate whether he plays at the Bucs. The former 49ers wideout has yet to record a catch this season, but his almost 50 percent of offensive snaps in Week 1 mean he very likely could get involved moving forward. He'll face a Bucs defense that's ranked top 10 (24.9 PPR points per game) against wide receivers so far this season.

free_agents.name: Wil Lutz
free_agents.outlook: Wil Lutz has been perfect to begin the season for the Broncos, and in a Week 2 win over the Jaguars, he converted both his field-goal attempts and both his PATs. The veteran kicker has been consistent since following Sean Payton northwest from New Orleans, and kicking at altitude has allowed him to be reliable from long range, but the Denver offense doesn't provide him with enough opportunities to be among the elite at his position. Lutz will face a Rams team in Week 3 that just kept the Giants out of the end zone but which has allowed five FG attempts through two games.

free_agents.name: AJ Barner
free_agents.outlook: AJ Barner should again lead Seattle's TE corps in a Week 3 tilt versus Washington. Barner logged a healthy 56 of the Seahawks' 70 offensive snaps Sunday versus the Cardinals, but he finished with just one catch (on one target) for eight yards. Barner did boost his fantasy line considerably with a rushing touchdown, though his three catches for 21 yards through two weeks isn't going to turn many heads. Nonetheless, he could be a sneaky option for Week 3 against a Commanders defense that has already given up four receiving TDs to tight ends, tied for most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Chig Okonkwo
free_agents.outlook: Chig Okonkwo did not play in Week 2 for the Commanders. Washington's active tight ends did not fare well, catching a combined two passes for 20 yards in the 37-20 loss to Dallas. Starting quarterback Jayden Daniels only played a half due to injury, and veteran backup Marcus Mariota will likely start in Week 3 versus a devastating Seattle defense. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per game thus far in 2026, which is second in the league. Seattle is also allowing the fewest passing yards per contest at 124.5 per tilt. None of this appears to be a recipe for success for Okonkwo, even if he is able to suit up.

free_agents.name: Jacoby Brissett
free_agents.outlook: Jacoby Brissett will look to bounce back from a poor performance when Arizona faces the 49ers in Week 3. Brissett recorded just 95 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception Sunday in a loss to Seattle, with that yardage being less than half of his previous low mark across any of his 16 starts for the Cardinals. Still, McBride was able to maintain his rapport with star tight end Trey McBride, as the pair connected for 41 yards and a touchdown through the air. Brissett's path to a rebound isn't an easy one, as San Francisco has given up just 11.8 fantasy points per game to QBs -- the second-fewest in the league -- through two weeks.

free_agents.name: Pat Bryant
free_agents.outlook: Pat Bryant fell back to earth after a promising season opener, failing to catch his only target in the Broncos' Week 2 win over the Jaguars. Quarterback Bo Nix made it a priority to get Jaylen Waddle going, and there wasn't much volume available for anyone else. Bryant gained 16 rushing yards on his only carry, but the No. 3 role in the Denver passing game doesn't figure to offer consistent production, and Bryant could face a challenge for the job once Marvin Mims overcomes a foot injury. Bryant will face a Rams secondary in Week 3 that's allowed just 19 receptions to WRs through two weeks, tied for seventh in the NFL, but three of them have gone for touchdowns.

free_agents.name: Gunnar Helm
free_agents.outlook: Gunnar Helm is tied for second on the Titans with seven targets through two games, but he has just 41 receiving yards. The 2025 fourth-round pick is locked in as the team's starting TE heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants, who just allowed six catches for 54 yards and a TD to Rams TE Terrance Ferguson. Helm is unlikely to match that production considering he has yet to exceed 51 receiving yards in a game while scoring just twice through 18 NFL appearances. Unless second-year Titans QB Cam Ward starts to pick up his passing production, Helm can continue to be ignored in the vast majority of fantasy formats.

free_agents.name: Nick Folk
free_agents.outlook: Nick Folk's early-season struggled could continue in the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers, who have allowed just 6.0 kicking points per game this season. Through two games in 2026, Folk has made just three of six field-goal tries, which is the worst mark in the NFL. He could benefit from the return of quarterback Michael Penix, however, who is expected to drive improvement after Atlanta's offense averaged just 8.0 points per game prior to his return.

free_agents.name: Xavier Hutchinson
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Hutchinson drew nine targets in Nico Collins' (hamstring) absence in Week 2 but turned that into just three catches for 37 yards. Hutchinson figures to maintain a prominent role in Houston's passing game against the league-worst Colts defense in Week 3, especially if Collins remains sidelined. Whether Hutchinson can turn that significant usage into production is another matter, as he has usually failed to capitalize on such opportunities in the past, with only two career regular-season games of 42 or more receiving yards. Hutchinson is in the Week 3 deep-league flex conversation, but his lack of prior production is concerning.

free_agents.name: Germie Bernard
free_agents.outlook: Germie Bernard and the Steelers host the Bengals for a Week 3 divisional showdown. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, the rookie stepped into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and Roman Wilson. Bernard caught four of eight targets for 35 yards in the 20-3 loss, seemingly earning the trust of Aaron Rodgers rather quickly. He led the team in yardage, was second in targets, and tied for second in receptions. Bernard faces Cincinnati's 9th-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (25.0) to WRs and should be considered a roster stash until we see this type of performance consistently.

free_agents.name: Kendrick Bourne
free_agents.outlook: Kendrick Bourne appears to have earned a key role in Arizona's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup versus San Francisco. After joining the Cardinals in the offseason, Bourne has recorded 11 targets through two weeks, second-most among Arizona wide receivers. The veteran wideout has logged a 10-86-0 line on those opportunities, as he has established good chemistry with QB Jacoby Brissett. With that said, Week 3 could be another tough test for Arizona's air game: the 49ers have allowed just a 59.3 percent catch rate to WRs so far, ninth-best in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Geno Smith
free_agents.outlook: Geno Smith will look to be the next quarterback to take advantage of the Lions' secondary when the Jets head to Detroit in Week 3. Smith hasn't topped 250 yards through two games and has just one touchdown pass, but he is in a very favorable spot in Week 3, with Detroit having allowed three touchdown passes in each outing thus far. Smith threw 41 times in Week 2, and so long as the Lions are scoring, Smith will likely have high volume again, putting him in a position to have his best showing of the year.

free_agents.name: Demarcus Robinson
free_agents.outlook: Demarcus Robinson suffered an ankle injury in San Francisco's win over the Dolphins on Sunday, and his status is very much in doubt for a Week 3 matchup against Arizona. Before getting hurt, Robinson caught all three of his targets for 34 yards against Miami as the 49ers' No. 3 wideout. In the likely scenario that he can't play in Week 3, Jacob Cowing would stand to step into Robinson's place in the pecking order. Arizona has given up four receiving TDs to wide receivers through two weeks, tied for the most in the league.

free_agents.name: Tre' Harris
free_agents.outlook: Tre' Harris caught only one pass in the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders, but he made it count, connecting with a scrambling Justin Herbert for a 53-yard gain that set up a third-quarter touchdown. Harris has just a 4-73-0 line on nine targets through two games, but if he continues to show he can gain significant yards after the catch, he could prove to be a good fit for OC Mike McDaniel's scheme. The 2025 second-round pick will face a Bills secondary in Week 3 that's given up the fourth-most receiving yards to WRs so far this year.

free_agents.name: Kirk Cousins
free_agents.outlook: Kirk Cousins has had an impressive start to the season, throwing three touchdowns in back-to-back games for a Raiders team that's a surprising 2-0. The veteran quarterback hasn't played completely mistake-free football under Klint Kubiak, throwing three interceptions, but he's only been sacked twice and has completed 67.8 percent of his passes. As long as Cousins remains productive and the team is winning, there will be little incentive for Las Vegas to hand the reins to rookie Fernando Mendoza, but that switch still figures to be coming at some point in 2026. Cousins will face a Saints defense in Week 3 that has done a good job holding Jared Goff and Lamar Jackson in check through its first two contests.

free_agents.name: Ryan Flournoy
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Flournoy managed six targets last game for Dallas. Flournoy parlayed those looks into five catches for 23 yards. Flournoy was third in targets behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Darren Waller
free_agents.outlook: Darren Waller could remain a valuable part of the Panthers' offense in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Through two games, Waller appears to be the Panthers' top receiving option at tight end, leading the TE room in yards (66), receptions (five) and touchdowns (two). However, having only received five targets through two weeks, Waller is likely a touchdown-or-bust streaming option going forward. He's in for a tough Week 3 matchup against a Browns defense that's given up just 10.5 PPR fantasy points per game to the position this season.

free_agents.name: Spencer Shrader
free_agents.outlook: Spencer Shrader has made all four of his field-goal attempts and five of six extra point tries through two games this season. The Colts are averaging a robust 26.5 points per game, but their success on offense has been overshadowed by a league-worst defensive performance en route to a 0-2 start. Shrader is gaining some streaming appeal heading into a Week 3 home game against the Texans, who are allowing 28.0 points per game in the early going after giving up just 17.4 points per game last season. He's a borderline fantasy starter at this point.

free_agents.name: Kaleb Johnson
free_agents.outlook: Kaleb Johnson could continue to carve out a role as the Packers take on the Falcons in Week 3. Johnson saw a huge uptick in usage against the Jets in Week 2, logging eight carries for 32 yards. The second-year ball carrier was the most efficient of Green Bay's RBs, and he could continue to see an early-down role if MarShawn Lloyd remains inefficient. Still, Atlanta has allowed a bottom-ten 127 rushing yards to running backs, which could make Johnson's job tough even if he's the Packers' go-to on the ground.

free_agents.name: DeMario Douglas
free_agents.outlook: DeMario Douglas' role in New England's struggling passing offense is questionable ahead of a Week 3 game at Jacksonville. In Week 2, Douglas logged just two targets in his first full game without A.J. Brown after a seven-target opener, and he's averaging just 4.8 yards per reception to start the season. Jacksonville is allowing a hefty 10.3 yards per target to opposing wideouts, but Douglas' inability to stretch the field would require uncharacteristic heavy volume to provide a modest fantasy return.

free_agents.name: Drew Lock
free_agents.outlook: Drew Lock could have another opportunity to lead Seattle's offense in Week 3 versus Washington. Lock started for the injured Sam Darnold (glute) on Sunday versus Arizona and threw for 235 yards with three touchdowns. Darnold is reportedly making good progress in his recovery, so it's not yet clear who will helm the team's offense in Week 3. Whichever QB gets the opportunity could be in for a big game against the Commanders, who have allowed a league-high seven passing touchdowns and have no interceptions through two weeks.

free_agents.name: Andy Borregales
free_agents.outlook: Andy Borregales' opportunities could again be limited when the Patriots face the Jaguars in Week 3. Borregales missed his first kick of the season in Week 2, and through two games, has just four field-goal attempts and three extra points as New England's offense has struggled to sustain drives. Jacksonville has allowed just three field goals and three extra points through two games, so there are likely more reliable Week 3 options.

free_agents.name: Greg Dulcich
free_agents.outlook: Greg Dulcich's opportunities have been limited in Miami's passing game heading into a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. Dulcich has four total catches on five targets to open the year, tallying 35 yards. Kansas City has allowed volume to the position through two weeks, surrendering 12 catches and two touchdowns, but just 74 total yards and 4.6 yards per target. Better fantasy options are available.

free_agents.name: Cade Otton
free_agents.outlook: Cade Otton is expected to remain Tampa Bay's top tight end in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Through two weeks, Otton is tied for the most targets (11) and second-most receptions (eight) on the Buccaneers, which is a good sign for his outlook moving forward. He's currently on pace to finish with career highs in targets (93) and receptions (68), though is role could diminish once Jalen McMillan returns to full speed. Otton is in for a difficult matchup in Week 3, as Minnesota's defense has allowed just 9.9 PPR fantasy points per game to TEs this season.

free_agents.name: Isaac TeSlaa
free_agents.outlook: Isaac TeSlaa will seek to stay involved as the Lions play the Jets in Week 3. TeSlaa recorded his first catches of the season against the Bills in Week 2, reeling in two of five targets for 26 yards. While his final stat line was still modest, the second-year receiver's five targets are promising. With that being said, he still hasn't done enough to be considered more than a depth option, especially against a New York defense that's been tougher on wide receivers so far this year.

free_agents.name: Jaylen Wright
free_agents.outlook: Jaylen Wright's role is limited in the Dolphins' backfield entering a Week 3 matchup with the Chiefs. He has logged just seven snaps through two games and is now dealing with a stinger issue that makes him uncertain to play. With no clear immediate path to touches, Wright is an insurance policy in a matchup against a defense allowing 4.0 yards per carry.

free_agents.name: Oronde Gadsden
free_agents.outlook: Oronde Gadsden hasn't logged much volume to begin the season, with just four targets through two games, but he's caught all four for 50 yards and scored his first touchdown of 2026 in the Chargers' loss last week to the Raiders. The second-year tight end's usage could increase significantly in the coming games. Both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar left the Week 2 loss to Las Vegas with injuries that are expected to land them on injured reserve, leaving Gadsden as the only healthy TE on the roster. He doesn't have the blocking skills of his veteran teammates, which could limit how much OC Mike McDaniel is willing to put him on the field, but Gadsden's workload will still increase almost by default unless the team is able to find immediate help from outside the organization. He'll face a Bills defense in Week 3 that ranks in the bottom 10 in catches and receiving yards allowed to tight ends this season.

free_agents.name: Keon Coleman
free_agents.outlook: Keon Coleman will look to build on a mild breakout when the Bills face the Chargers in Week 3. He hauled in six passes last week, his highest total since Week 1 of 2025, as the Bills lost DJ Moore (shoulder) early in Week 2. The Chargers have been more vulnerable to slot options than bigger outside receivers, and Moore's availability remains in flux. With the Bills offense clicking at all levels, Coleman can still garner enough volume to be a deep-league flex consideration.

free_agents.name: Deshaun Watson
free_agents.outlook: Deshaun Watson and the Browns host the Panthers for their home opener in Week 3. He completed 24 of 30 pass attempts for 238 yards with two TDs and no INTs, while rushing seven times for 22 yards during Cleveland's surprising Week 2 win over the Buccaneers. Watson led the comeback victory with scoring strikes of 55 and 17 yards, and chemistry appears to be brewing between him and the Browns' young playmakers. He'll face a Carolina defense that held the Falcons to 129 yards passing and forced three INTs and two fumbles in Week 2.

free_agents.name: Emari Demercado
free_agents.outlook: Emari Demercado continues to play backup to Javonte Williams following the Malik Davis injury, but Demercado has had a marginal role through the first two games for Dallas. Demercado has five carries for a combined 15 yards behind Williams. Even if he receives a few extra touches, Demercado will have a difficult time finding room in Week 3 versus Baltimore. The Ravens are allowing just 83.5 rushing yards per tilt, which is sixth in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Demond Claiborne
free_agents.outlook: Demond Claiborne is set to be a secondary option at running back once again as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Claiborne did not log a carry as one of Aaron Jones' backups against the Bears in Week 2, but he did reel in his single target for two yards. Still, the rookie running back will remain a depth pick against a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.

free_agents.name: Michael Penix Jr.
free_agents.outlook: Michael Penix is slated to make his 2026 debut during the Falcons' Week 3 matchup against the Packers. Atlanta has struggled offensively with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand as the team's quarterbacks over the last two weeks, scoring just 16 total points while Rush and Strand accounted for seven turnovers. However, Penix led the Falcons' offense to 20.6 points per game while throwing for 220.2 yards per game when healthy in 2025, suggesting improvement could be coming. Penix will be in for a tough matchup though, as Green Bay's defense has given up just 19.2 fantasy points per game to opposing QBs this season.

free_agents.name: Colby Parkinson
free_agents.outlook: Colby Parkinson has had a quiet start to the season heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. Parkinson logged just one catch Week 1 and followed that with a 2-15-0 receiving line on Monday Night Football. Meanwhile, fellow TE Terrance Ferguson put up a 6-54-1 line, proving that there's room for players at the position to thrive with QB Matthew Stafford -- though who that tight end is could vary on a week-to-week basis. Denver was burned by Travis Kelce for 71 yards in Week 1 but held Jaguars TEs to just 24 receiving yards in Week 2.

free_agents.name: Matt Gay
free_agents.outlook: Matt Gay has been busy to begin his Raiders' career, converting all three of his field-goal attempts and all six of his extra points through the first two games of the season. The outlook for the offense should improve once Brock Bowers is cleared for his 2026 debut, and while there's additional uncertainly on the horizon once first overall pick Fernando Mendoza is deemed ready to replace Kirk Cousins under center, Gay could actually benefit if the young QB struggles to get the ball into the end zone while he figures out NFL defenses. Gay will face a Saints team in Week 3 that's allowed an exact mirror to his production so far, with opposition kickers getting three FGs and six PATs.

free_agents.name: Xavier Legette
free_agents.outlook: Xavier Legette is expected to play a depth role in Carolina's receiving corps in the Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Legette had a solid Week 2 performance after putting up a goose egg in Week 1, catching two of four targets for 64 yards. The third-year pro remains firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker in Carolina's receiving corps, as the two have combined for 26 receptions, 380 yards and a touchdown through two weeks. However, Legette could take advantage of a Cleveland secondary that's allowed 10.0 yards per target to opposing WRs heading into Week 3.

free_agents.name: KaVontae Turpin
free_agents.outlook: KaVontae Turpin did not even garner a target last game for Dallas. Turpin continues to be utilized largely in the return game. Meanwhile Ryan Flournoy is the clearcut No. 3 wideout behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. In Week 3, Dallas hosts the Baltimore Ravens. Baltimore is allowing just 191 passing yards per contest, which is 12th in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Konata Mumpfield
free_agents.outlook: Konata Mumpfield's role in the Rams' Week 3 matchup against Denver could depend on the status of Puka Nacua (hip). With Nacua sidelined Monday versus Denver, Mumpfield drew the start, but he finished with just one catch on two targets for 12 yards. Meanwhile, Davante Adams posted a massive 10-195-2 line, with no other Los Angeles wideout reeling in more than one catch. The Broncos won't be an easy matchup in Week 3, as they've held opposing WRs to an average of just 13.2 fantasy points per game this season, fourth-fewest in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Cole Kmet
free_agents.outlook: Cole Kmet remains a depth option as the Bears play the Eagles in Week 3. Even though Kmet played more offensive snaps in Week 2 (69 percent) than in Week 1 (57 percent), he garnered just one target and was unable to catch it. Still, young tight end Colston Loveland has yet to do much this year, which could keep a veteran presence like Kmet relevant. He'll face a Philly defense that's allowed the fewest PPR fantasy points per game to tight ends this season (5.1).

free_agents.name: Daniel Carlson
free_agents.outlook: Daniel Carlson is expected to have few scoring opportunities in the Saints' Week 3 matchup against the Raiders. Carlson, who spent the previous eight seasons with the Raiders, converted on all three of his field-goal tries during the Week 2 win over the Ravens. He could continue to receive scoring opportunities due to New Orleans' offensive success. However, Carlson is likely in for a difficult Week 3 matchup, as Las Vegas has allowed just 4.5 kicking points per game this season.

free_agents.name: Ollie Gordon II
free_agents.outlook: Ollie Gordon's workload could increase if Jaylen Wright misses the Dolphins' Week 3 game against the Chiefs. Despite being No. 3 on the depth chart, Gordon has outsnapped Wright behind Miami's workhorse, De'Von Achane. Kansas City allowed stud Jonathan Taylor to rush for two scores in Week 2 but kept Denver's backs under control in Week 1. Barring an injury to Achane, it's difficult to envision a path to meaningful production for Gordon.

free_agents.name: Seth McGowan
free_agents.outlook: Seth McGowan is locked in as the little-used backup to workhorse Colts RB Jonathan Taylor, having beaten out DJ Giddens (knee) for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. McGowan has just two carries and one target through two games. With Taylor healthy for a Week 3 home game against the AFC South rival Texans, McGowan remains a non-factor in fantasy.

free_agents.name: Jack Bech
free_agents.outlook: Jack Bech has been unable to escape a supporting role in the Raiders' offense to begin his second NFL season. Through two games, the 2025 second-round pick has a 5-48-1 line on just six targets, volume that will make it very difficult to make a consistent impact. Bech had to watch journeyman Cody White come off the practice squad and catch two red-zone TDs in a Week 2 win over the Chargers, and the impending return of Brock Bowers will bump everyone else down a rung in the pecking order for looks. Bech seems unlikely to break out in Week 3 against a Saints secondary that ranks in the middle of the pack in terms of volume allowed to wide receivers so far, but which has given up three TDs to the position in two games.

free_agents.name: Jahan Dotson
free_agents.outlook: Jahan Dotson is expected to operate as Atlanta's No. 2 wideout in the Week 3 matchup against the Packers, whose defense has allowed just 8.3 yards per completion this season. Despite Dotson clearly operating as the Falcons' No. 2 wideout this season, he's had little fantasy value, in large part due to the problems at quarterback. With Michal Penix set to return in the Week 3 matchup, Dotson could be more relevant but will likely remain overshadowed by Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson. Dotson could find the end zone, however, as the Packers' defense has already allowed three touchdowns to wideouts in two games, which is tied for the fourth-most in the NFL.

free_agents.name: Ted Hurst III
free_agents.outlook: Ted Hurst is expected to remain one of the Buccaneers' top receiving options in the Week 3 matchup against the Vikings. Despite the return of Jalen McMillan in the Week 2 loss to the Browns, Hurst played a career-high 45 offensive snaps -- 38 more than McMillan. Additionally, Hurst led the team with seven targets, though it led to just two receptions. Regardless, it appears as if Hurst will remain an important piece of the Buccaneers' offense as the season progresses. The rookie wideout will likely struggle but could find success against a Minnesota secondary that's allowed 12.6 yards per completion this season.

free_agents.name: Ryan Fitzgerald
free_agents.outlook: Ryan Fitzgerald is expected to have plenty of scoring opportunities in the Panthers' Week 3 matchup against the Browns. Fitzgerald has started the season strong, converting on all three of his field-goal tries and eight of nine point-after attempts. Additionally, he could continue to benefit from the Panthers' offensive success, as the team currently ranks second in points per game (35.5). Fitzgerald is in for a great Week 3 matchup as well, with Cleveland allowing 11.5 kicking points per game through two contests this season.

free_agents.name: Tyquan Thornton
free_agents.outlook: Tyquan Thornton produced strong numbers in Kansas City's Week 2 overtime win over the Colts, hauling in all four of his targets for 86 yards. The fifth-year speedster is at best fifth in the pecking order for looks from Patrick Mahomes, but his role as a deep option gives Thornton some big-play potential in the right matchup, even on limited volume. He'll face a Dolphins defense in Week 3 that's given up five passing TDs through two games, but only one to a wide receiver.

free_agents.name: Sione Vaki
free_agents.outlook: Sione Vaki should remain Detroit's low-usage RB2 in Week 3 against the Jets. Vaki logged one carry for seven yards and caught one pass for 13 yards against the Bills in Week 2, showcasing that the secondary running back for the Lions is a graveyard role this year. The third-year ball carrier is still on pace to log career-high numbers given his small role so far in his career, but he's nothing more than a depth option with Jahmyr Gibbs healthy.

free_agents.name: Roman Wilson
free_agents.outlook: Roman Wilson and the Steelers welcome the division rival Bengals to town for a Week 3 matchup. With Michael Pittman (foot) on the sidelines last Sunday, Wilson stepped into the No. 2 receiver role behind DK Metcalf. He finished the 20-3 loss with a team-high five catches for 28 yards on six targets. Rookie Germie Bernard was one of Aaron Rodgers' favorite receivers, however, turning eight targets into four catches and a team-leading 35 yards. Pittman's status is cloudy at best for Week 3, but Wilson and the Steelers face a Cincinnati defense allowing 25.0 fantasy points per game (9th) to WRs, so he's best left on benches for now.

free_agents.name: Joey Slye
free_agents.outlook: Joey Slye has been limited to two or fewer field-goal attempts in 12 of his last 13 outings for the Titans, who continue to have one of the league's worst offenses. After averaging 16.7 points per game last season, Tennessee is scoring 15.0 PPG heading into a Week 3 road game against the Giants. It's a favorable matchup on paper since the Giants are banged up on both sides of the ball, but MetLife Stadium tends to have some of the least-favorable weather conditions for kickers, and Slye's upside will continue to be capped by the Titans' inability to consistently move the ball on offense. There are better kicking options available for fantasy.

free_agents.name: Raheim Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Raheim Sanders and the Browns host the Panthers in Week 3. He tallied two carries for four yards and caught his only target for seven yards during Cleveland's first win of the season in Week 2. Quinshon Judkins handled 12 of 15 carries by running backs, and as long as he remains healthy, the workload split should remain similar. Sanders does have some upside as a receiver out of the backfield, but his role is still too limited to be relied upon in fantasy. Carolina's defense has been susceptible on the ground, allowing 36.3 fantasy points to RBs (31st), but they rank 14th in receiving yards surrendered to the position.

free_agents.name: Chad Ryland
free_agents.outlook: Chad Ryland will hope for Arizona's offense to find more success in Week 3 against San Francisco. The Cardinals managed just seven points Sunday in a loss to Seattle, and Ryland's only scoring opportunity was a successful extra point on that score. He was much more active in Week 1, when he made four of five FG attempts and both PAT tries. The 49ers have given up an average of only 10.0 points through two games, so Ryland may see limited opportunities again in Week 3.

free_agents.name: Drew Stevens
free_agents.outlook: Drew Stevens missed his second field goal of the season last game for Washington. Stevens did make two other field goals as well as both of his PATs, but the Commanders offense is not a pretty option for a fairly shaky kicker heading into a brutal Week 3 matchup versus Seattle. The Seahawks are allowing just 8.5 points per contest thus far this season, which is second in the NFL. In addition, starting quarterback Jayden Daniels is unlikely to play for the Commanders after dislocating his elbow.

free_agents.name: Emanuel Wilson
free_agents.outlook: Emanuel Wilson will look to build upon a big performance when Seattle faces Washington in Week 3. With Jadarian Price suffering a shoulder injury against Arizona on Sunday, Wilson stepped up and led the Seahawks with 21 rushes for 92 yards. Price's injury isn't considered serious, but it's not certain that he'll be able to return to action in Week 3. Whoever leads Seattle's backfield will be looking to score the first rushing touchdown against the Commanders this season.

free_agents.name: Will Shipley
free_agents.outlook: Will Shipley managed nine touches for 29 yards in Week 2 versus the Titans after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger injury. Saquon missed portions of the game due to the ailment, leaving his status in question for Week 3 versus the Bears. Barkley is slated to undergo an MRI to determine if he will miss any time. Shipley and Tank Bigsby would likely split touches if Barkley cannot go, with Bigsby getting the slight edge, as the latter had 15 touches and a touchdown to outpace Shipley. In Week 3, the Eagles will face a Bears run defense allowing 122 yards per clash on the ground, which is 22nd in the league.

free_agents.name: Andrei Iosivas
free_agents.outlook: Andrei Iosivas and the Bengals are on the road for a Week 3 meeting versus the Steelers. He caught his only target for seven yards during Cincinnati's Week 2 victory, and it looks like that could be his norm moving forward. Iosivas played 54% of offensive snaps after playing 61% in the season opener. He's clearly behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins in the receiver pecking order and thus should remain on waiver wires in Week 3 against Pittsburgh's second-ranked passing defense.

free_agents.name: Jason Sanders
free_agents.outlook: Jason Sanders appears on track to serve as the Jets' kicker again in Week 3 at Detroit. Despite Blake Grupe being on the roster, Sanders has been the active option through two games, hitting four extra points and four of five field goals. Volume is questionable as the Jets' offense isn't highly efficient, and Detroit's defense has allowed just two field goal attempts while surrendering nine touchdowns.

free_agents.name: Kyle Williams
free_agents.outlook: Kyle Williams hopes for more opportunities in Week 3 as the Patriots face the Jaguars. Rising up the depth chart with A.J. Brown on IR, Williams still only recorded a 21% snap share, registering two targets and a 10-yard catch in Week 2 where New England completed only 14 passes. Williams has big-play potential, but the passing game isn't operating at a high enough level to sustain a No. 4 WR despite facing a defense that's allowing 10.3 yards per target.
